items.body:
# Central agent handoff — 8 October 2026

**Read first:** [ASSPS consolidated governance report](https://github.com/HassiMian/app-assps-edu-pk/blob/coord/assps-four-stream-consolidation-20261008/docs/coordination/CHAT_CONSOLIDATION_AND_AGENT_GOVERNANCE_20261008.md) and the four `*_MASTER_HANDOFF.md` documents on the same documentation-only branch.

Only four active development chat/workstreams: (1) Paper Studio, including Paper Workspace, printing, Early Years, Lesson Planning, Diary and approved bank **consumption**; (2) Grade IX–X Academic Question Bank, independently verified provenance and **approval**; (3) SaaS Core & Production, sole release/DB/RLS owner; (4) APEX Connect, role-aware SaaS client/projection, **not** separate source-of-truth.

**Observed, not permanent:** live frontend `9fe7b560`, backend `16ab8f34` on 2026-10-08 13:08Z; release anchor `68a158e`. Grade 9/10 research `1b29218` not academically approved. Lesson/Diary candidate `2b10eab` not deployed. This handoff only documents ownership; production untouched.

**Every agent must preflight:** verify live component metadata, source ancestry and clean worktrees; claim feature paths/owner; preserve other agents' work; record exact test/role/RLS/print and rollback evidence. Core alone promotes to production after gates. The Academic stream sends only independently approved revision-bound snapshots to Paper Studio. Never use old chat instructions as deployment authority.

Related unfinished issues: [#1](https://github.com/HassiMian/app-assps-edu-pk/issues/1) Curriculum-Paper contract, [#2](https://github.com/HassiMian/app-assps-edu-pk/issues/2) Phase3AE, [#3](https://github.com/HassiMian/app-assps-edu-pk/issues/3) serial+statement selection. Do not close them merely because this coordination issue exists.

**Chat history:** Group eligible old chats in ChatGPT Projects, keep one MASTER per stream, archive rather than delete after unique-history verification. These docs are NOT a physical ChatGPT chat merge; no automatic confirmation of other independent agents receiving or acknowledging this notice.

items.body:
<!-- local-draft: artifacts/local-ai/out/issue-draft-obligations-assessor.md -->
## Summary

Create a dedicated Claude Code agent, `test-obligations-assessor`, that decides per file, per line and per test flag (unit, guard, contract, property, integration) which test obligations apply, whether a target of 0 is legitimate, and what the demanding-and-realistic targets and their justifications are. It records a verdict in the coverage manifest and is mandatory in worker briefs, SPEC-003 audits, the zero review and doubtful areas, always as a party distinct from the code's author. Decided by the maintainer on 2026-10-26 as option (D) of #2890 (agent for judgment plus deterministic syntax tripwire).

## Motivation

- Use cases and scenarios: Today targets are chosen by whoever writes the code or the brief; zero unit/guard/contract targets are accepted for files with executable code and nothing can tell (#2840), and 22 package/flag pairs have no package target while a 0 per-file target reports as met (#2841).
- Industry comparison: A deterministic gate cannot judge context (is this 0 legitimate? is 60% demanding enough for this branching?); an agent can, but acts only when invoked and is not reproducible. The maintainer's decision pairs both: the agent judges, the tripwire of #2890 (Roslyn syntax analysis against a closed list of non-executable constructs) fails CI when a 0-target file gains executable lines, or when a file under `src/` has no verdict or a verdict older than the file's last change. Together nobody can skip the agent and no verdict can silently go stale.
- Strategic context: EPIC #2845 (measurement integrity); AGENTS.md section 9 (obligations are justified, demanding and realistic); the obligations policy of 2026-10-05; #1762 (justifications in the manifest); #1763 (rule (b) of the test-auditor). A distinct assessor removes the author's incentive to set low targets and gives the audit pipeline one owner for obligations.

## Proposed Solution

- Agent definition `.claude/agents/test-obligations-assessor.md`: model Sonnet (effort high, because reasoning is the job), tools PowerShell, Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write. Read-only on `src/` and `tests/`; the only file it writes is the verdict inside `.github/coverage-manifest/{Package}.json` (and its own report under `artifacts/`). Hooks follow `.claude/agents/test-auditor.md` (block-worker-publish, block-main-checkout-writes, block-prohibited-commands, enforce-path-ownership with `-Agent test-obligations-assessor`, no-background-specialists, block-worker-spawn). Never pushes, opens PRs or issues. It also needs a lessons file `.claude/agents/lessons/test-obligations-assessor.md` and a row in `.claude/agents/README.md` (agent table and delegation table).
- Verdict format, recorded per file in `.github/coverage-manifest/{Package}.json`: per flag a `target`, a one-sentence `justification` tied to the file's code, a `verdictDate` (yyyy-MM-dd) and an `assessor` (agent name and run id); for a line-level argument, a list of lines or ranges with the reason they are raised or lowered. A legitimate 0 carries the reason and the closed-list construct (if any) it relies on. The schema extension is shared with #2890's tripwire, which reads `verdictDate` and compares it with the file's last git change.
- The assessor may argue raising or lowering obligations for specific lines and test types, not only whole files.
- Integration points:
  - `worker-brief` skill: a brief for any `src/` change has a mandatory step "assessor verdict before code"; the worker reads the verdict and the PR reports measured coverage against it.
  - `issue-audit` skill, test stage: the assessor runs next to `test-auditor` on the scope list and its verdicts are the baseline for the obligations findings (rule (b)).
  - `pr-cycle` skill: before the PR is opened, files touched under `src/` have a current verdict.
  - Zero review of EPIC #2845 and doubtful areas: the assessor reviews every 0 target.
  - Spawn-hook enforcement: a hook denies spawning an `issue-worker` on a brief that touches `src/` unless the brief records the assessor step (or a verdict newer than the files' last change exists), and the assessor must be a different spawn from the worker that authors the code.
- Relation to other issues: #2890 is the deterministic tripwire that consumes the verdicts (closed list of non-executable constructs, CI failure on missing or stale verdict); #2840 (zero targets accepted for files with executable code) and #2841 (package/flag pairs without target) are the debts the assessor and tripwire make visible and fix; EPIC #2845 is the parent.
- Implementation plan required before work: `docs/plans/test-obligations-assessor-implementation-plan-<issue>.md` generated with the plan prompt `docs/engineering/prompts/implementation-plan-prompt.md` and linked from this issue (AGENTS.md section 11).

## Alternatives Considered

List every implicit choice of this feature (defaults, error semantics, storage, public names, behaviour on missing context, dependencies, ordering, retention) and classify each one:

- **Trivial**: follows a cited convention.
- **Settled**: the only option that complies, with a verifiable citation (an `AGENTS.md` section or rule, a SPEC id, an ADR number, a law article, a link to an earlier maintainer decision, or named comparable products). Write the choice and its citation; do not present it as an open option.
- **Dilemma**: two or more valid options, each better in a concrete named scenario. Write each option with its pros and cons and the scenario where it wins. Only an issue with a Dilemma carries the `needs-decision` label.

Zero Dilemmas is valid: write "No open design choices" and keep the settled choices with their citation.

1. **Judgment by an agent plus deterministic tripwire** (Settled): maintainer decision of 2026-10-26 on #2890, option (D). Cited: https://github.com/dlrivada/Encina/issues/2890 (decision comment).
2. **Model Sonnet with high effort** (Trivial): follows the routing rule in `.claude/agents/README.md` (Sonnet with high effort only where reasoning is the job, as for `issue-auditor`).
3. **Verdict stored in the coverage manifest, not in a separate file** (Settled): the maintainer decision states "Its verdicts are recorded in the coverage manifest, where this issue's tripwire checks them"; `AGENTS.md` section 9 makes the manifest the source of per-file targets and justifications.
4. **Assessor is always a party distinct from the code's author** (Settled): same maintainer decision.
5. **Read-only on `src/` and `tests/`** (Trivial): follows `test-auditor` ("Analysis only: never change src/, tests/ or docs/").

No open design choices.

## Affected Packages

Which Encina packages would this feature affect? None of the library packages.

> Retour de test du PO du 16/09/2026 — demande tracée dans #804.

## Contexte

Le PO : « les staffs doivent avoir un aperçu de leur emploi du temps ». Ce
ticket livre l'API. L'écran « Mon planning » fait l'objet d'un ticket distinct.

## Constat

- Le jeton ne porte que `userId`, `tenantId` et `role`
  (`identity/identity.types.ts:36-40`).
- Aucun code ne relie un compte à sa fiche praticien : la relation
  `User.staffProfiles` n'est lue nulle part hors du schéma, et
  `StaffMemberDto` masque `userId` (`catalog/dto/staff.dto.ts:148`).
- `GET /v1/appointments/mine` filtre sur `clientId` : c'est l'historique d'une
  cliente (`appointments.controller.ts:247-266`).
- `GET /v1/appointments?staffId=` existe, mais le filtre est choisi par
  l'appelant, pas imposé par le jeton.

## Critères d'acceptation

1. `GET /v1/me/staff-profile` rend la fiche praticien du compte connecté, ou
   404 `STAFF_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND` si le compte n'en a pas.
2. `GET /v1/me/appointments?from=&to=` rend les rendez-vous du praticien
   connecté :
   - le `staffId` est **dérivé du jeton**, par la clé `(tenantId, userId)` de
     la table `staff`, jamais lu dans un paramètre ;
   - la plage est bornée à 31 jours et le tri est chronologique ;
   - chaque rendez-vous porte son créneau en UTC avec offset, son statut, sa
     prestation (nom et durée), la cliente (prénom et initiale du nom), la
     note laissée par la cliente et la note interne du salon.
3. `GET /v1/me/schedule?from=&to=` rend, sur la plage, les horaires récurrents
   du praticien, ses absences et les jours de fermeture du salon.
4. Un `staffId` passé en paramètre est refusé en 400, comme champ inconnu : le
   périmètre ne se choisit pas.
5. Tests d'intégration :
   - un praticien du salon B ne voit rien du salon A ;
   - un praticien ne voit pas les rendez-vous d'un collègue ;
   - un compte MANAGER sans fiche praticien reçoit 404.
6. Le contrat est décrit dans `packages/shared` par des schémas Zod
   (ADR 0008).

## Références

CDC §1.3 (« Outils de coordination d'équipe → Comptes staff, rôles,
disponibilités »), §1.4 et §2.4 · `.claude/skills/tenant-isolation/SKILL.md`

> Retour de test du PO du 16/09/2026 — demande tracée dans #804.

## Contexte

Le personnel et les clientes ont désormais des comptes à mot de passe. Un
produit vendu doit leur permettre de **récupérer un accès perdu** sans passer
par le support.

## Constat

- Aucune route de réinitialisation n'existe ; le code le signale lui-même
  (`identity/users.controller.ts:246-248`).
- Pour un praticien, le seul recours est une nouvelle invitation émise par un
  ADMIN. Pour une cliente, il n'y en a aucun.

## Critères d'acceptation

1. `POST /v1/auth/password-reset` reçoit `{ tenantSlug, email }`. Il répond
   **toujours 202**, que le compte existe ou non, et limite le débit par IP et
   par adresse.
2. Le jeton de réinitialisation :
   - est aléatoire, d'au moins 256 bits ;
   - est stocké haché ;
   - ne sert qu'une fois et vit 30 minutes ;
   - est invalidé par l'émission d'un nouveau jeton et par tout changement de
     mot de passe.
3. `POST /v1/auth/password-reset/confirm` reçoit `{ token, password }`. Il
   applique la politique de mot de passe et révoque tous les refresh tokens du
   compte.
4. Le message part par la chaîne de notifications (modèle `password_reset`,
   canal e-mail). Le lien pointe vers `/{slug}/admin/mot-de-passe` ou vers
   `/{slug}/compte/mot-de-passe`, selon le rôle du compte.
5. Tests :
   - un jeton émis pour le salon A est refusé sur le salon B, sans révéler son
     existence ;
   - un jeton ne se rejoue pas ;
   - un jeton expiré est refusé ;
   - une adresse inconnue produit la même réponse qu'une adresse connue.
6. Un compte suspendu, ou un compte d'un établissement désactivé, ne reçoit
   rien (voir #407).

Dépend de #799

CDC §2.3 (authentification des clients, du staff et des administrateurs) ·

items.title: Postgres CDC: error when syncing inherited tables where child has different schema than parent
items.body:
### Summary
When running Postgres CDC with `PEERDB_POSTGRES_CDC_HANDLE_INHERITANCE_FOR_NON_PARTITIONED_TABLES` enabled and the source uses old-style `INHERITS` tables (not declarative partitioning), child tables with **extra columns** beyond the parent's schema cause tuple decoding failures or cross-child data corruption.

Unlike partitioned tables where all partitions share an identical column layout, `INHERITS` children can add their own columns (e.g. `stripe_payment` inherits 18 columns from `payment` and adds `fk_stripe_payment` and `stripe_account_id`). The WAL emits tuples using the child's column layout, but PeerDB was decoding them using the wrong RelationMessage.

### Root cause
When a child table's `RelationMessage` arrived in the WAL stream, `processMessage` mutated `msg.RelationID` from the child's ID to the parent's:
```go
msg.RelationID, err = p.checkIfUnknownTableInherits(ctx, msg.RelationID)
```
This caused `processRelationMessage` to store the child's RelationMessage under the **parent's** relation ID:
```go
p.relationMessageMapping[currRel.RelationID] = currRel  // stored under parent's ID
```
Then in `processInsertMessage` / `processUpdateMessage` / `processDeleteMessage`, the RelationMessage was looked up using the parent's ID:
```go
rel, ok := p.relationMessageMapping[relID]  // relID = parent's ID
```
This had two consequences:
1. **Cross-child contamination**: multiple children's RelationMessages overwrote each other under the same parent key — whichever child sent last determined the column layout used for all children.
2. **Positional mismatch**: a child with extra columns (e.g. 20 columns) had its tuple decoded using a RelationMessage from a different child or the parent (e.g. 18 columns), causing columns to be decoded with the wrong types.

### Fix
- Stop mutating `msg.RelationID` in the `RelationMessage` handler. Store each child's RelationMessage under its **own** relation ID.
- In `processInsertMessage` / `processUpdateMessage` / `processDeleteMessage`, use the child's actual relation ID (`actualRelID`) for RelationMessage lookup (correct tuple decoding), and the parent's relation ID (`relID`) only for table name and destination routing.
- In `processRelationMessage`, resolve to the parent via `getParentRelIDIfPartitioned` for name/schema lookups, but leave `currRel.RelationID` untouched for storage.

items.title: [Note] AI Engineer
items.body:
## AI Engineer 能力地圖：Frame × 關鍵字

以下以每個 frame 作為領域；每個關鍵字一列，欄位固定為一句話理解、概念、技術、實作、情境、注意；「一句話理解」以 Full Stack 工程師熟悉的系統開發視角說明。

### Data Engineering

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ETL / ELT | 像後端資料搬運管線：抽取資料、整理格式，再送進分析系統。 | 把來源資料可靠地送到分析層；ETL先轉換、ELT先落地再轉換。 | 批次/增量、CDC、schema evolution、Spark/dbt。 | 以Airflow排程、dbt轉換、資料品質檢查與重跑機制落地。 | 報表、數據同步、資料湖到倉庫。 | 避免全量重跑；處理重複、遲到資料、PII與schema變更。 |
| Data Warehouse | 專門給報表與分析查詢的集中式資料庫。 | 面向分析的集中式資料儲存，重視一致性與查詢效能。 | 星型模型、分區、columnar storage、OLAP。 | 建立raw/staging/mart分層與維度/事實表。 | BI、KPI、跨來源報表。 | 不要把交易庫直接當分析庫；控管成本與資料新鮮度。 |
| Data Lake / Lakehouse | 像大型物件儲存倉庫，但加上可查詢、版本與治理能力。 | 保留大量原始資料並兼顧治理與分析能力。 | Object storage、Parquet、Delta/Iceberg、schema-on-read。 | 以bronze/silver/gold分層，設定catalog、partition與compact。 | 半結構化資料、ML訓練、歷史留存。 | 小檔案與無治理會拖垮查詢；需管理版本、權限與生命週期。 |
| Streaming / Real-time | 把資料當事件即時處理，類似 WebSocket 或 queue consumer。 | 資料事件產生後即時處理，而非等待批次窗口。 | Kafka/PubSub、Flink/Spark Streaming、watermark、幂等。 | 設計topic/schema、consumer group、checkpoint與DLQ。 | 即時告警、推薦、即時儀表板。 | 至少一次不等於不重複；處理順序、背壓、遲到事件與重放。 |
| Data Modeling | 替資料設計可長期維護的 schema、關聯與統計口徑。 | 把業務實體、關係與指標轉成可查詢且可演進的結構。 | 正規化/反正規化、維度建模、SCD、data contract。 | 先定義grain，再建立主鍵、外鍵、指標與欄位字典。 | 跨團隊共用資料、報表與特徵。 | grain不清會造成重複計算；避免只為當下報表硬編模型。 |
| Data Quality & Governance | 替資料加上測試、ownership、權限與可追溯性。 | 確保資料正確、完整、及時、可追溯且有人負責。 | 契約測試、expectations、lineage、catalog、SLA。 | 在pipeline加入schema、null、範圍、freshness與異常告警。 | 重要報表、監管資料、ML輸入。 | 品質規則要可執行；告警過多會被忽略，需訂責任人與處置流程。 |
| Orchestration | 像 CI/CD workflow，負責安排資料任務的順序、重試與排程。 | 管理資料工作流的依賴、重試、排程與可觀測性。 | DAG、Airflow/Dagster、sensor、backfill、retry。 | 任務保持冪等，設定timeout、重試、依賴與失敗通知。 | 多步ETL、每日報表、模型pipeline。 | 不要把業務邏輯塞進排程器；避免隱性依賴與無限重試。 |

### RAG / LLM Application

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture | 把 ingestion、搜尋、LLM 與 API 拆成有清楚邊界的服務。 | 定義RAG元件如何串接、資料流如何走，以及同步/非同步邊界。 | Retriever-generator pipeline、API gateway、cache、queue。 | 拆 ingestion、retrieval、generation、evaluation 與 serving。 | 企業知識問答、客服、文件搜尋。 | 先定義延遲、成本、權限與失敗降級，再選框架。 |
| Chunking | 把長文件切成模型搜尋得到、又看得懂的小段落。 | 把文件切成適合檢索與模型上下文的片段。 | 固定長度、語意切分、recursive splitter、overlap。 | 依標題/段落切分，保留metadata並用檢索指標調整大小。 | 長文件問答、規章與技術文件。 | 切太小失去上下文，切太大降低召回；不要切斷表格與程式碼。 |
| Embedding | 把文字轉成可比較相似度的數字向量。 | 將文字轉成向量，讓語意相近內容在向量空間靠近。 | Transformer embedding、cosine similarity、批次embedding。 | 固定模型與版本，建立向量索引並記錄embedding model。 | 語意搜尋、相似案例、RAG召回。 | 模型換版需重建索引；多語、領域詞與向量維度要驗證。 |
| Vector DB | 替 embedding 建索引，讓系統能快速做語意搜尋。 | 儲存與查詢向量及其metadata的資料庫。 | HNSW/IVF、ANN、top-k、filter、Qdrant/pgvector/Milvus。 | 建立collection、索引、metadata filter與刪除/更新流程。 | 大量文件的語意檢索。 | top-k不是品質保證；注意索引更新、租戶隔離與查詢成本。 |
| Metadata Filtering | 像 SQL WHERE，先用權限、租戶或日期縮小搜尋範圍。 | 先用結構化條件縮小可檢索範圍，再做語意搜尋。 | 欄位filter、ACL filter、tenant_id、時間/版本條件。 | 把權限與來源metadata寫入chunk，檢索時強制套用。 | 依部門、產品、日期、權限搜尋。 | filter不能由模型自由決定；缺metadata會造成越權或漏召回。 |
| Hybrid Search | 同時跑關鍵字搜尋和語意搜尋，再合併結果。 | 結合關鍵字精確匹配與向量語意匹配。 | BM25、dense retrieval、rank fusion、RRF。 | 並行查詢兩路召回後融合、去重並評估權重。 | 專有名詞、編號與自然語言混合查詢。 | 只用向量容易漏掉ID/術語；融合權重需用資料驗證。 |
| Reranker | 像搜尋結果的第二輪排序器，把真正相關的內容往前排。 | 對初步召回結果重新排序，提升前幾筆相關性。 | Cross-encoder、Cohere rerank、top-N reranking。 | 先取較大的candidate pool，再對前N筆重排。 | 召回很多但答案常不在前幾筆。 | 會增加延遲與成本；不要把reranker當作權限層。 |
| Query Rewriting | 把使用者模糊的問題改寫成更容易查到資料的查詢。 | 把模糊、口語或多輪問題改寫成更適合檢索的查詢。 | Query expansion、multi-query、HyDE、conversation rewrite。 | 保留原問題，產生候選查詢並記錄改寫結果。 | 追問、省略主詞、跨語言與複雜問題。 | 改寫可能改變原意；需防止注入與錯誤擴張。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| Faithfulness | 檢查答案是否真的有文件證據支持。 | 答案是否能被提供的上下文支持，而非模型自行捏造。 | Citation checking、NLI、LLM-as-judge、groundedness。 | 要求引用來源，逐句比對claim與context並設拒答門檻。 | 法規、客服、內部知識問答。 | 有引用不代表真的支持；避免把judge分數當絕對真值。 |
| Hallucination | 模型講得很像真的，但內容其實沒有依據。 | 模型產生與證據不符或不存在的內容。 | Grounding、temperature control、answer abstention、fact check。 | 無證據時拒答，輸出引用與信心，記錄錯誤案例回歸。 | 資料不完整或問題超出知識庫。 | 降低temperature無法根治；需改善召回與輸出驗證。 |
| Failure Modes | 列出系統會怎麼壞，並預先設計偵測、降級與復原。 | 系統在資料、檢索、模型、工具或網路異常下的失敗型態。 | Failure taxonomy、chaos test、timeout、retry、DLQ。 | 建立錯誤分類、fallback、告警與可重現測試案例。 | 上線前演練與事故分析。 | 只測happy path不夠；重試可能放大流量與費用。 |

### Agent

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Workflow | 像後端狀態機，把 Agent 任務拆成可控制的步驟。 | 把Agent任務拆成可追蹤、可重試、可控的步驟。 | State machine、DAG、LangGraph、workflow engine。 | 明確定義節點輸入輸出、轉移條件與終止條件。 | 多步研究、客服處理、資料操作。 | 避免讓模型自行決定所有流程；限制迴圈與最大步數。 |
| Tool Calling | 讓模型用結構化參數呼叫 API，而不是只產生文字。 | 讓模型以結構化參數呼叫外部工具完成工作。 | Function calling、JSON schema、tool registry。 | 驗證參數、套用權限、執行工具並把結果回傳模型。 | 查詢API、寄信、寫入資料庫。 | 工具呼叫等同權限操作；需白名單、審計與人工核准。 |
| State | 保存 Agent 做到哪裡、拿到什麼結果，以及下一步要做什麼。 | 保存Agent在多步任務中的上下文、結果與目前階段。 | State schema、checkpoint、短期/長期記憶。 | 用明確schema儲存狀態，支援重試、恢復與版本遷移。 | 長流程、多輪對話、非同步任務。 | 不要把所有對話無限塞進prompt；避免狀態污染與競態。 |
| Planning | 讓 Agent 先拆任務再執行，但每一步仍要驗證。 | 先決定子任務與執行順序，再逐步完成目標。 | ReAct、plan-and-execute、task decomposition。 | 限制計畫深度，逐步驗證工具結果並允許重新規劃。 | 研究、複合查詢、跨系統流程。 | 計畫不是事實；每一步都需驗證，並防止無限重新規劃。 |
| Guardrails | 像 middleware 與 policy layer，限制模型與工具能做什麼。 | 在輸入、工具、輸出各階段限制Agent可做的事。 | Policy engine、schema validation、content filter、allowlist。 | 建立前置/後置檢查，違規時拒絕、修正或轉人工。 | 高風險自動化、金融、客服。 | 只做輸出過濾不夠；工具層和資料層也要防護。 |
| Human-in-the-loop | 高風險動作先停住，交給人核准後才繼續。 | 在高風險或不確定步驟由人審核、接管或核准。 | Approval gate、confidence threshold、escalation。 | 設計待審佇列、審核理由、逾時與回滾流程。 | 付款、刪除、對外發信、敏感回答。 | 人工介入點要可量化；避免所有案件都卡在人工作業。 |
| Structured Output | 要求模型回傳符合 JSON Schema 的資料，方便程式接續處理。 | 要求模型輸出可被程式可靠解析的固定結構。 | JSON schema、Pydantic、constrained decoding。 | 解析後做schema與業務規則驗證，失敗則修復或重試。 | API回應、分類、工作流節點。 | 格式正確不代表內容正確；限制欄位長度與注入內容。 |
| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |

### LLM Evaluation

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |

| Evaluation | 像單元測試與回歸測試，但測的是 AI 回答品質。 | 用可重複的案例與指標衡量檢索和生成品質。 | Recall@k、MRR、faithfulness、answer relevancy、LLM judge。 | 建立golden set、版本化評測並在CI執行回歸測試。 | prompt、模型、chunk策略比較。 | 單一分數會掩蓋失敗類型；要分檢索、生成與安全評估。 |
| LLM Judge | 用另一個模型依評分規則批改 AI 回答。 | 用另一個模型依評分規準評估回答品質。 | Rubric、pairwise judge、calibration、human agreement。 | 固定prompt與模型版本，抽樣人工複核並監控偏差。 | 大量離線回歸、主觀品質評估。 | judge有偏見與位置效應；不要只依賴單一judge。 |
| Golden Dataset | AI 版本的固定測試案例與標準答案。 | 代表真實使用情境、具標準答案或評分規準的固定案例集。 | Versioned dataset、stratified sampling、edge cases。 | 標記來源、難度、語言與失敗類型，納入CI與變更審查。 | 模型/提示詞版本比較。 | 資料過時會誤導；要避免資料洩漏與只收集簡單案例。 |
| Observability | 把 metrics、logs、traces 串起來，看懂線上系統發生什麼。 | 讓團隊知道系統發生什麼、品質如何、成本多少。 | Metrics、logs、traces、dashboards、alerts。 | 關聯request id、tenant、model、prompt版本與結果指標。 | 線上除錯、SLA與容量規劃。 | 避免記錄原始敏感prompt；指標需能對應行動。 |
| Tracing | 像 distributed tracing，追蹤一次 AI 請求經過的所有步驟。 | 追蹤一次請求跨模型、檢索、工具與服務的完整路徑。 | OpenTelemetry、span、trace ID、Langfuse/Phoenix。 | 每個節點建立span，記錄輸入輸出摘要、耗時、token與錯誤。 | 定位慢點、錯誤與幻覺來源。 | trace資料可能含機密；設採樣、遮罩、保留期限。 |

| Latency | 拆解使用者等候時間，找出慢在 queue、搜尋、模型或工具。 | 從請求到回應的時間，需拆分各階段觀察。 | p50/p95/p99、TTFT、streaming、timeout。 | 分別量測queue、retrieval、LLM、tool與post-process。 | 互動式聊天、SLA設計。 | 平均值會掩蓋尾延遲；重試與串行工具會放大等待。 |

### Multi-tenant

| 關鍵字 | 一句話理解 | 概念 | 技術 | 實作 | 情境 | 注意 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Multi-tenant Architecture | 同一套後端服務多家公司，但每家的資料與資源必須隔離。 | 同一平台服務多個租戶，同時共享效率與隔離安全。 | Shared service、tenant context、quota、policy。 | 每個request注入tenant context，所有資料與快取操作強制帶租戶。 | SaaS型AI平台。 | 租戶邊界必須端到端驗證，不能只靠前端參數。 |
| Tenant Isolation | 確保任何查詢、快取、檔案與向量都不會跨租戶。 | 防止一個租戶讀寫另一個租戶的資料與資源。 | Logical/physical isolation、ACL、RLS、network policy。 | 在資料庫、快取、向量庫、物件儲存與日誌都套隔離。 | 共享基礎設施的SaaS。 | 要測越權與錯誤租戶context；背景任務也要帶tenant。 |
| Tenant ID | 像 request context 的主鍵，必須一路帶過 API、DB、queue 與 log。 | 識別請求所屬租戶並貫穿整個資料流。 | JWT claims、request context、composite key。 | 由可信身份來源取得，寫入資料表、trace、queue與cache key。 | 多租戶API與非同步工作。 | 不可信任使用者自行傳入的tenant_id；防止IDOR。 |
| Shared Database / Shared Schema | 所有租戶共用表，用 tenant_id 與 RLS 做隔離。 | 所有租戶共用資料庫與schema，以成本換取隔離複雜度。 | tenant_id、RLS、composite index、partition。 | 所有表加tenant_id，Repository層強制篩選並做隔離測試。 | 大量小租戶、成本敏感SaaS。 | 漏一個where就可能資料外洩；索引與熱租戶需特別處理。 |
| Database per Tenant | 每個租戶一個資料庫，隔離更強但維運成本更高。 | 每個租戶使用獨立資料庫，隔離與客製化較強。 | Database provisioning、migration orchestration、connection pool。 | 自動建立/升級/備份資料庫並管理租戶路由。 | 少量大型或合規租戶。 | 運維與連線成本高；migration與跨租戶分析更複雜。 |

| Horizontal Scaling | 增加更多相同服務實例來處理更高流量。 | Horizontal Scaling在系統架構中的核心問題與設計邊界。 | queue、cache、事件、限流與容錯；以Horizontal Scaling相關指標驗證取捨。 | 在系統架構流程中建立可測試、可監控的Horizontal Scaling模組。 | 高流量與非同步系統中的Horizontal Scaling使用情境。 | 注意一致性、故障邊界、背壓與觀測；需用測試、權限與告警避免失控。 |
| Observability | 把 metrics、logs、traces 串起來，看懂線上系統發生什麼。 | 讓團隊知道系統發生什麼、品質如何、成本多少。 | Metrics、logs、traces、dashboards、alerts。 | 關聯request id、tenant、model、prompt版本與結果指標。 | 線上除錯、SLA與容量規劃。 | 避免記錄原始敏感prompt；指標需能對應行動。 |
| Distributed Systems | 多個服務與節點共同完成工作，因此要處理網路、同步與一致性問題。 | Distributed Systems在系統架構中的核心問題與設計邊界。 | queue、cache、事件、限流與容錯；以Distributed Systems相關指標驗證取捨。 | 在系統架構流程中建立可測試、可監控的Distributed Systems模組。 | 高流量與非同步系統中的Distributed Systems使用情境。 | 注意一致性、故障邊界、背壓與觀測；需用測試、權限與告警避免失控。 |

> 來源：Miro board 的 10 個 frame；內容以 Full Stack 工程師理解 AI 工程能力地圖為目標整理。

## AI 系統從建置到上線：三段流程

閱讀順序只有三段：**先準備資料 → 再處理使用者請求 → 最後用線上結果持續改善**。底部三項是每個階段都必須具備的系統能力。

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph PREP["A. 事前準備：把資料變成 AI 可用的知識"]
    direction LR
    DE["1. Data Engineering<br/>收集、清理、治理資料"]
    DS["2. Data Science<br/>分析資料、定義指標與特徵"]
    ML["3. ML 基礎<br/>選模型、Embedding 與推論方式"]
    KB[("可檢索知識庫<br/>Chunks + Metadata + Vectors")]
    DE --> DS --> ML --> KB
  end

  subgraph REQUEST["B. 線上請求：使用者問問題時，系統實際怎麼跑"]
    direction LR
    USER["使用者 / 前端"] --> API["API 接收問題"]
    API --> RAG["4. RAG / LLM Application<br/>找資料、排序、組 Prompt"]
    RAG --> NEED{"需要執行動作？"}
    NEED -->|否| ANSWER["LLM 產生答案"]
    NEED -->|是| AGENT["5. Agent<br/>規劃步驟、呼叫工具、保存狀態"]
    AGENT --> ANSWER
    ANSWER --> USER
  end

  KB -->|提供相關資料| RAG

  subgraph IMPROVE["C. 上線後：觀察結果並持續改善"]
    direction LR
    OBS["6. Production AI / Observability<br/>記錄品質、延遲、成本與錯誤"]
    EVAL["7. LLM Evaluation<br/>Golden Dataset、Judge、Faithfulness"]
    FIX["修正資料 / Prompt / 模型 / 流程"]
    OBS --> EVAL --> FIX
  end

  ANSWER -->|留下 Trace 與 Feedback| OBS
  FIX -->|重新發佈| RAG
  FIX -->|補資料與品質規則| DE

  CROSS["所有階段共同要求<br/>8. Multi-tenant：租戶與資料隔離<br/>9. AI Security / Reliability：權限、PII、Guardrails<br/>10. Architecture：Queue、Cache、Scaling、Fault Tolerance"]
```

items.body:
> Volet non livré du deuxième critère de #824, laissé ouvert par la PR #1024 —
> hors de l'empreinte de ce ticket-là.

## Constat

**Le défaut d'origine de #824 est encore à l'écran.** Sa capture montre le tunnel
de réservation sans compte refusant « 06 12 34 56 78 » avec « numéro attendu au
format international. » — et c'est toujours le cas.

#824 a normalisé les **six** portes où le pays de l'établissement est lisible au
moment de l'écriture : inscription, profil, compte du personnel, invitation,
fiche cliente, réglages. La septième — la réservation invitée — normalise, mais
**sans pays par défaut** :

- `guestContactSchema` valide `phone` avec `e164PhoneSchema`
  (`packages/shared/src/schemas/appointment.ts`), c'est-à-dire
  `e164PhoneSchemaFor()` sans argument ;
- le schéma est monté sur le paramètre du handler par `ZodValidationPipe`, qui
  est **construit à l'amorçage de l'application**, une fois pour toutes. Il ne
  voit donc pas `tenants.country_code`, qui est une donnée de requête ;
- le formulaire de coordonnées d'`apps/web` valide avec le même schéma
  (`apps/web/app/(booking)/[tenantSlug]/reservation/steps/contact-step.tsx`), si
  bien que le refus tombe déjà dans le navigateur.

L'écart est donc **visible et incohérent pour une même personne** : le
« 06 12 34 56 78 » que `POST /api/v1/auth/register` accepte sur un salon français
est refusé par `POST /api/v1/public/{tenantSlug}/appointments` du même salon. Le
tunnel public est en outre le parcours le plus fréquenté du produit, et celui où
un refus coûte une réservation (CDC §1.4, boucle « réserver → confirmer »).

Le pays est pourtant **là** : le tunnel est résolu par slug dans l'URL, et
`PublicTenantResolver` a déjà posé l'établissement dans le contexte de requête
quand le corps est validé.

## Pourquoi #824 ne l'a pas fait

Parce que le combler demande trois emplacements, tous hors de l'empreinte qui lui
était confiée (`api/crm`, `api/identity`, `apps/api/prisma/migrations`,
`contracts:shared`) :

| Emplacement | Ce qu'il faut y faire |
|---|---|
| `apps/api/src/common/validation/` | un pipe à **portée de requête** qui instancie le schéma avec le pays du contexte, là où `ZodValidationPipe` le fige à l'amorçage |
| `apps/api/src/modules/appointments/` | monter ce pipe sur le handler du tunnel invité, à la place du schéma statique |
| `apps/web/.../reservation/steps/contact-step.tsx` | valider avec le pays de l'établissement, que la page connaît déjà |

Les trois doivent bouger **ensemble** : resserrer ou relâcher l'un sans les
autres déplace le refus après la soumission, sous la forme d'un message global en
tête de page pour un numéro que le champ venait d'accepter — ce que la skill
web-frontend §4 interdit, et ce que l'en-tête d'`e164PhoneSchema` documente
depuis #66.

## Critères d'acceptation

1. Un pipe de validation à portée de requête existe dans
   `apps/api/src/common/validation/`, monté par une fabrique qui reçoit le pays
   du contexte de tenant. Il conserve la garde `.strict()` de
   `ZodValidationPipe` — un `tenantId` glissé dans le corps reste refusé
   (tenant-isolation §2) — et lève le même tableau de messages, donc le même
   corps `{ code: "VALIDATION_ERROR", details.violations }`.
2. `POST /api/v1/public/{tenantSlug}/appointments` accepte « 06 12 34 56 78 » sur
   un établissement dont `country_code` vaut `FR`, et enregistre
   `+33612345678` — la même valeur que `POST /api/v1/auth/register` sur ce salon.
3. Le même corps sur un établissement **sans** `country_code` rend 400 : le pays
   ne se devine pas, et il ne traverse pas la frontière de l'établissement.
   Un établissement `MG` complète `034 12 345 67` en `+261341234567`.
4. Le formulaire de coordonnées d'`apps/web` applique la même règle **avant
   soumission** : le refus s'affiche sous le champ, jamais en bloc en tête de
   page (web-frontend §4). Le libellé d'aide cesse d'exiger l'indicatif quand
   l'établissement a un pays.
5. Un test d'isolation inter-tenant couvre le cas : le pays lu est celui du slug
   de l'URL, jamais celui d'un autre établissement.
6. `guest-booking-frontier.spec.ts` est mis à jour — son cas
   « `0341234567` refusé » devient « accepté et normalisé » pour un salon
   malgache, et le refus sans pays reste couvert.
7. La capture de #824 ne se reproduit plus à 360 px.

## Références

- #824 — la normalisation des six autres portes (PR #1024), et sa capture
- #66 — la répartition initiale entre `phoneSchema` et `e164PhoneSchema`
- #404 / ADR 0008 — « le contrat Zod valide, la classe DTO documente », et la
  reprise progressive dont ceci est un reste
- `apps/api/src/modules/identity/phone.ts` — l'en-tête décrit l'écart et ce
  qu'il faudrait pour le refermer

items.title: [RFC] Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse for Agentic/RAG Workloads
items.body:
### **Summary**

RadixAttention reuses KV cache only when a request's prefix is byte-identical and at the same absolute offset as something already cached. In agentic/RAG traffic shared system prompts, tool schemas, retrieved documents, and multi-turn history routinely put identical content at different offsets across requests. This causes a guaranteed cache miss even though the content itself hasn't changed.

_Three recent approaches tackle this differently. Wanted to check if this is on anyone's radar before digging further._

- **Irminsul** ([arXiv:2605.05696](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.05696)) (sglang-targeted but no code). Exploits MLA's factorization into a position-free latent ($$c_{KV}$$) and a small rotatable slice ($$k_r$$). The idea is that reusing a cached span at a new offset only requires a closed-form "delta-rotation" on the small rotatable slice. it is  MLA-specific,  though the same split exists in any partial-RoPE model (rotary_dim < head_dim), not just MLA, so the mechanism plausibly generalizes further than the paper states explicitly. 

- **MiniPIC** ([arXiv:2606.13126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13126)) ( vLLM).  Stores unrotated K, defers RoPE to attention-read-time. More general ( RoPE models) but touches every attention backend, conflicts with fused write-path kernels, and needs new per-token position plumbing through CUDA-graph-captured decode. Code exists ([IBM/vllm](https://github.com/IBM/vllm), traced to the actual authors' commits). It is worth knowing that it went through two implementation strategies, and the first one ([PR #88](https://github.com/IBM/vllm/pull/88)) shipped with an acknowledged accuracy bug from concurrent requests reusing the same span at different positions, serious enough that they abandoned it for a different strategy rather than patch it. Real, useful precedent for anyone attempting this class of feature. In principle this can be applied on top of sglang, but requires substantial engineering. I wonder if it is worthwhile.

- **COMB** ([arXiv:2602.01519](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01519)) — a third, different category: trains a dedicated encoder component into the model rather than changing only the inference engine. Claims 51-94% TTFT reduction, 3x throughput, tested on DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat. Code released: [github.com/shijuzhao/Comb](https://github.com/shijuzhao/Comb).

### **What's been looked into so far**

Confirmed against current sglang code that RoPE is baked into K at write time and the radix-cache hash chain is explicitly position-coupled.  today's architecture can't do any of the above without new work. All three are recent (Feb-June 2026) with limited independent validation, so there are potential bugs, 

I searched existing issues/PRs and didn't find prior discussion of this specific angle. Closest related work is #27574 / #24656 (agent-aware/session KV cache hints), but that's a different problem targeting cache locality/lifecycle, not reuse across a shifted position with identical content.

**Questions for the community**

Has anyone evaluated any of these for sglang already, even informally?
Is there a reason this hasn't come up that isn't obvious from the papers?

Would a narrow, opt-in delta-rotation implementation (gated to MLA/partial-RoPE models, feature-flagged behind a --radix-cache-backend variant) be a welcome contribution, or better suited as an external/experimental extension?

Happy to share more detailed technical notes if there's interest.

The earlier body-barrier nondetection remains a service-defense masking observation, not a product leak. ### Final integration evidence

Canonical local gate on final composed `82a7bad1170f7394650537d8e10540a2f02590ce`: **76 executed / 0 carried / PASS**, including fresh native SDK4 and the separate active-export case. Manifest SHA-256: `40971a65a53bce28d7092c94be9b88d5f290fdb6c2ae1fb2f344cc97366e41a1`.

The [published 24-case / 566.7-second exploration](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/issues/1612#issuecomment-6099834717) retains **23 passing cases and one strict offered-schedule failure**. Missing those measurements does not reopen the completed source-function scope; no universal SLO, three-repeat rule or blanket matrix is added.

The detailed historical record below is preserved. Historical checklists are not a second current task list. Security, durability, immutable-original and fail-closed guarantees remain in force; no unperformed quantitative, environmental or release claim is marked qualified. All seven applicable exact-main workflows passed (29 successful checks, 11 expected skips), including [Go](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/actions/runs/37204816309), [CodeQL](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/actions/runs/37204816351), [Admin](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/actions/runs/37204816359), [Node](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/actions/runs/37204816338), [Rust](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/actions/runs/37204816326) and [Dart](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/actions/runs/37204816367). The 74-step mandatory local gate, 99 Admin browser contract cases and 26 CI contract tests passed; real Server Connect tests remain distinct from the browser fixture. Local manifest SHA-256: `1fdfb42c91eaeb803c7ce2a6e863b0a17459f9497b04a574b12f6b03281163d5`; exact-main completion proof SHA-256: `a29eb2c08c623641f9c151cc72285ec4685fac916811a13c620120f3e61d48c1`.


## Superseding Edge policy decision — Head managed

The user adopted the Head-managed Edge model on 2026-10-04: base read is tail VertexRead AND head VertexRead; modification is tail VertexRead AND head VertexWrite. Explicit Deny/default deny remain. Independent directed prefix-pair Role configuration is withdrawn; #1626 now owns the concrete effect/response/compatibility matrix. Query/CDC/export/receipt capabilities remain independent. Head write does not grant VertexDelete or endpoint creation/update. HA new Create stays disabled.

Previous directed-policy candidate #1649 and its passing local results remain historical evidence, not qualification of this new policy. The user selected typed blind acceptance for head write-only callers. It acknowledges authorized request handling without claiming mutation success or disclosing weight/existence/collision/results. SDKs must explicitly represent unavailable details; batch/count/receipt/idempotency and current permission changes obey the same rule. Role/schema/ADR and runtime work proceed under this decision. Kubernetes/Helm remains deferred; native HA/security stays in scope.

Part of #1599.

**Depends on:** #1603.

## Problem

#1599 requires prefix access isolation inside query execution. Search candidates and traversable paths need authorization before top-k/traversal; search snapshots need Principal/policy ownership and scan cursors need confidential progress. Filtering final results is insufficient. Ranking statistics intentionally remain shared within the existing corpus.

## Scope

- Collection scans/keys-only/counts use requested scope intersected with Allow scopes minus Deny. Apply visibility before limits/counting/pagination; entirely unauthorized scopes fail without inspecting data.
- Prefix Delete/dry-run explicitly selects only authorized victims, uses the same lifecycle predicate for both modes, applies limits afterward, and reports no denied counts/identities. Exact batches retain whole-request rejection.
- Authorized induced graph for BFS/PPR/community/degree and reductions: authorize the seed; hidden vertices/edges are never traversable bridges or returned resources. TF-IDF/BM25 base weights reuse shared corpus statistics. PPR transitions and community cuts normalize/accumulate only traversable edges; scope-dependent destinations and final scores are expected. Degree/weighted-degree reports count only admitted incident edges.
- Search restricts matching candidates before scoring/top-k/retained-hit limits. Reuse the existing index's precomputed field/class DF, N and length totals; private data within that same corpus may change visible scores/order. Do not build per-Role/Principal ranking-statistics caches or maintain their invalidation/journals. Keep bounded posting/permission bitmap intersection for candidate selection.
- Physical query budgets include rejected postings/adjacency to preserve bounded work and cancellation. Hidden edges never enter traversal normalization. Public authorized traversal exhaustion errors reveal the reason without physical scan counters.
- Opaque integrity-protected cursors bind deployment, Principal, request/scope, policy revision/generation and the necessary storage progress. Role/scope changes invalidate continuation. Existing retained search snapshots remain node-local unless explicitly redesigned; reject foreign-node cursors or preserve deliberate affinity.
- Scoped BackupSnapshot requires data-read plus export permissions and returns only the authorized induced graph, with current-policy checks during the stream.
- Ops/global metrics require separate Role capabilities; a namespace-reader does not gain deployment totals or peer diagnostics.
- Do not expose any unprotected algorithm to restricted Roles while this task is incomplete.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Real-wire nested Deny scopes in scans/counts/dry-run/delete/export with limits and pagination.
- [ ] Hidden high-degree/bridge/document mutations never disclose denied resources or create paths through them; actual counts, aggregates and paging remain scoped. Visible ranking may change through shared corpus statistics.
- [ ] Shared statistics agree after update/delete/TTL maintenance/restore. Compare first and reused scopes plus read/write mixtures for search and graph traversal, recording time, allocations and retained-memory bounds.
- [ ] Different graph/index corpora never share statistics; sys-only changes cannot influence business scores/counts/topology.
- [ ] Seed denial, synthetic PPR edges, projection/reduction, cursor theft/Role change/scope change, and node-local search affinity.
- [ ] Export revocation terminates within the declared bound without further data; benchmark authorized views.
## Delivery rules

Every changed external behavior needs same-PR real Connect integration coverage for a happy path and a failure/edge contract. Add hot-path benchmark scenarios where applicable. Preserve the module DAG, focused provider sub-configs, plural-canonical writes, and source/test pairing. Regenerate all affected consumers; never hand-edit generated code. Run the mandatory local gates before any push. Write all Issue content and updates in English.

- Cursor confidentiality requires authenticated encryption or random server-side handles. Base64/signatures alone are insufficient. Unfiltered data/candidate/actual-count fast paths require effective permission for every required action/resource across the entire domain with no applicable Deny; an empty-prefix Allow or security-admin Role alone is insufficient. Shared ranking statistics within the existing corpus are deliberately independent of this condition.

## Namespace and execution cost
Business index projection analyzes logical data keys/values, not physical data: syntax, and excludes sys: at ingestion/statistics. Global fast paths refer only to the data domain; sys-only mutations cannot affect public score/count/topology.
Compile disjoint Allow ranges minus Deny and skip denied subtrees before limits/counting. Avoid cloning/reindexing or recomputing permission-specific DF/N/lengths per request. Use constrained adjacency and matching-posting/candidate bitmap intersections. Core understands generic ranges and its own corpus statistics, never OIDC/Role policy. Existing GraphCache/index instances remain corpus boundaries; no tenant partition is inferred from a key prefix. Protected result/page caches include scope/policy/content versions and relevant natural TTL expiry, with bounded memory. Retained search pages keep stable snapshots but revalidate policy/authority before protected output. Measure query allocations and writer lock delay.


## Final performance preflight and next prerequisite

Finding from final #1661 acceptance preflight (#1610/#1612): Final performance preflight is held: the arm64 Docker VM has 16 CPUs and 8,216,018,944 B memory, while host load is 24.18/26.92/26.61 with six existing development containers. This does not meet the quiet-host prerequisite. No new final image/capacity run occurred and no existing container/job was changed. Private preflight manifest SHA-256: `a631af997f69ec4c66233f5c53eee59d302ddcf06791ab00a61734feccf520e4`; frozen exact-main source archive SHA-256: `337058a99264f0df8ac245e6c29de9d6e6883e0c9dcabb60b7a7700ae18dbb2f`. This is preparation, not a passing performance sample. Next: qualified quiet-host preflight, one pinned image and the predeclared unchanged final matrix.

No final-source performance exit is completed. Core diagnostics and all real-wire/source/CI proofs remain retained; Google/provider, physical-device and publication exits are separate, with Dart releases last.

Remaining comparative-path prerequisite: current `testbed/bench/run.sh` creates `-mode off` for non-receipt scenarios; its ghz path is plaintext and unauthenticated. `shared_ranking.yaml` explicitly remains a diagnostic with a query prefix, not proof of OIDC admission. Before final #1610/#1612 OFF/ON acceptance, qualify an actual protected Role-bound comparative path with matched logical data, TLS/topology and offered load, first/warm/update-mixed Search/BFS/PPR/Community plus allocations/retained/peak memory and writer delay. Preserve diagnostic/release workloads and floors; a passing OFF scenario cannot qualify protected scope. Source: [native mode selection](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/blob/93d537892f3025d4a1666dcab36c5748d5cfb9f6/testbed/bench/run.sh#L275), [shared ranking scenario](https://github.com/anaregdesign/lantern/blob/93d537892f3025d4a1666dcab36c5748d5cfb9f6/testbed/bench/scenarios/shared_ranking.yaml). This prerequisite belongs to the existing final matrix, not a change to production auth or the frozen integration cohort.



</details>

items.title: Build QueueStore with the guarded upsert as the only write path

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified; claimable by any session

items.body:
## Current context

**Current state:** GitHub records this issue as closed.

**Context:** QueueStore is the shared database module that owns the queue projection and related state. A guarded upsert inserts or updates only when an incoming task version is newer; HOLDLOCK is the SQL Server lock hint used to serialize the same-key decision. **Why it matters:** duplicate, delayed, or concurrent messages must not replace a newer queue row with stale state.

**Outcome:** The issue is closed after PR #188. The guarded QueueStore path, equal-version behavior, concurrency evidence, and documented HOLDLOCK decision passed the recorded CI checks.

**Repository evidence:** [#188](https://github.com/collaborationwithothers/cdc-platform-azure/pull/188) (merged 2026-08-27)

## Unknowns

The merged PR has CI evidence for the declared tests. That evidence does not claim Azure production concurrency or performance beyond the container boundary.

## Historical evidence

The original issue body is retained below unchanged. It preserves the original behavior, blockers, paths, verification method, acceptance checklist, scope boundaries, size forecast, dates, and links.

<details>
<summary>Original issue body</summary>

## Behavior

Queue-builder needs one current queue row for every task. `Lexfield.QueueStore` is the shared database module that owns those rows and the tables used by the reconciler and notifier.

Every task change carries a version number. QueueStore writes the change only when its version is newer than the version already stored.

```text
Stored:   tenant-a, task 42, state QA, version 7
Incoming: state Assigned, version 5
Result:   ignore version 5 and keep the version 7 row unchanged

Incoming: state Completed, version 8
Result:   replace the row because version 8 is newer
```

This single rule makes late repair results and duplicate event delivery safe. Old data cannot replace new data.

The live event path and reconciler repair path can both try to create the same missing task row. The guarded write must let both calls complete without a duplicate-key error or deadlock and must leave one row at the higher version.

## Blocked by

- [x] #36 (T1)
- [x] #68 (`docs/agents/writing-style.md` correction-ratchet path)

## Paths

- `src/Lexfield.QueueStore/`
- `tests/Lexfield.QueueStore.Tests/`
- `tests/Lexfield.TestSupport/ContainerFixtures.cs`
- `tests/Lexfield.TestSupport/Lexfield.TestSupport.csproj`
- `tools/onboarding/Lexfield.Onboarding.csproj`
- `docs/specs/21-src-queue-builder.md`
- `docs/agents/writing-style.md`
- `src/Lexfield.slnx`

## Verification

Method: containers

Run the QueueStore tests against Testcontainers SQL Server. The suite must create all six tables, reject lower and equal versions, and repeat the same-missing-row writer race 30 times. Every repetition must finish without a duplicate or deadlock, leave exactly one row, and keep the higher version.

## Acceptance checklist

- [x] `QueueState`, `SentNotifications`, `dbo.StreamAttribution`, `ReconcilerWatermark`, `DriftObservation`, and `SweepLease` all exist in the migration
- [x] The guarded upsert is the only public write path; no method writes a row without the version guard
- [x] An out-of-order write at a lower version leaves the row unchanged
- [x] The concurrent-writer test passes repeatedly, not once
- [x] V12's recorded answer is linked from the comment that explains the chosen statement shape
- [x] Every direct `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient` project reference uses 6.1.6
- [x] The QueueStore decision record preserves the MERGE scale caution, the caller-owned retry boundary, and readable source formatting

## Out of scope

- Running a Kafka consumer
- Calling the task-api repair route
- Implementing the reconciler sweep
- Sending notifications

## Size forecast and measurement

Current measured PR size: 11 files; 471 additions; 75 deletions; 546 total changed lines.

This exceeds the normal file-count and line-count gates. Hari approved `large-pr-approved` on PR #188. The exception keeps the package alignment and correction-ratchet documentation in this ticket, and avoids compressing public prose to manufacture a smaller count.

---

Area: `src/queue-builder` | Wave 2 | Plan id `B1` | Generated from `docs/specs/` by /to-tickets.

</details>

items.title: Define actor and caller provenance for delegated and app-only task writes

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified; claimable by any session

items.body:
## Current state

Open and unblocked, with no linked implementation pull request. Issues #40 and #68 are closed, so no blocking edge remains. Actor and caller provenance for delegated and app-only task writes is not settled or verified. Provenance means the recorded identity and invocation path that explain who caused a write and on whose behalf. The current issue remains a design question rather than a runtime contract.

## Context

This concerns task-api writes in the multi-tenant workflow path, including user-delegated calls and application-only service calls that may cross an authorization boundary.

## Why this matters

A task transition must be attributable without confusing the calling application with the human or delegated principal. Leaving this undefined weakens audit, authorization review, and incident diagnosis.

## Historical evidence

The text below is retained from the original issue as historical evidence and planning context. For open work, unchecked acceptance items and unmerged plans are not evidence of completion.

> *This was generated by AI during triage and refined after deciding that v1 supports both delegated-user and app-only task writes.*

### Pre-change contract and decisions


This section records the pre-change contract and decisions as historical evidence. It is not the current runtime state.

Issue #40, implemented by merged PR #171, exposed the original trust mismatch. Task creation derives actor from the authenticated JWT `NameIdentifier` or `sub` claim. Task transition accepts actor in the request body and records it in both `WorkflowTask.UpdatedBy` and the outbox event.

The current HTTP contract explicitly lists actor in the transition body. ADR-001 requires business facts such as actor and intent to remain recoverable downstream. ADR-004 includes actor in the delta event. Neither document currently defines user, workload, client, OBO, or application-permission provenance.


## Behavior

Task creation and transition support two authorization modes:

1. Delegated access, including direct user calls and OAuth on-behalf-of (OBO) calls.
2. Application access, including client credentials and managed identity calls.

Every committed task write records two independently useful identities derived only from the validated access token:

- `actor`: the user or workload whose token subject performs the operation.
- `clientApplicationId`: the immediate client application that called task-api.

The event also records `permissionMode` as `delegated` or `application`.

The canonical actor identifier is:

- `user:{tid}:{oid}` for delegated access.
- `workload:{tid}:{oid}` for application access.

`tid` and `oid` come from the validated token. The v2 `azp` claim, or v1 `appid` claim, supplies `clientApplicationId`. Endpoint code reads the validated claims principal and never parses the raw `Authorization` header.

Neither a request-body field nor a custom HTTP header can set or override any provenance field. The transition request no longer includes `actor`. A request that still supplies the legacy body field returns 400 so the caller cannot mistake ignored input for trusted attribution.

`WorkflowTask.UpdatedBy` stores the same canonical actor identifier written to `TaskTransitioned.actor`. Its current `nvarchar(64)` width cannot hold the longest canonical value, so the implementation follow-up must widen it to `nvarchar(128)`. The outbox event adds `clientApplicationId` and `permissionMode`.

Task creation must stop using `"unknown"` as a fallback.

## Flow semantics

| Flow | Actor | Client application | Permission mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Direct delegated user | `user:{tid}:{oid}` | `azp` or `appid` of the direct client | `delegated` |
| OBO through a middle tier | `user:{tid}:{oid}` | `azp` or `appid` of the immediate middle tier | `delegated` |
| Client credentials | `workload:{tid}:{oid}` | `azp` or `appid` of the calling application | `application` |
| Managed identity or workload federation | `workload:{tid}:{oid}` | `azp` or `appid` of the calling workload application | `application` |

OBO does not accept a represented user from request data. The validated downstream token already carries the user subject and identifies the middle-tier client.

An app-only operation has no user actor. If a user initiated an asynchronous job earlier, the executing workload remains the actor. Preserving the earlier user requires separately trusted causation data created when the job was accepted. That future causation contract is not a body or header override of actor.

Support impersonation and other explicit representation flows are not supported in v1. A future representation contract must record the authenticated operator, represented subject, client, authorization evidence, and reason separately.

## Authorization semantics

Token validation, permission authorization, tenant authorization, and attribution are separate checks.

- A missing or invalid access token returns 401.
- A token missing `tid`, `oid`, or both `azp` and `appid` returns 401 because task-api cannot establish required provenance.
- A token containing `scp` is treated as delegated. It must carry the documented task-write delegated scope.
- An app-only token has no `scp`. It must carry the documented task-write application role in `roles`.
- A valid token lacking the required delegated scope or application role returns 403.
- A valid and permitted token that fails the existing `TenantRoute` authorization returns 403.
- Delegated and application permission names must be selected and documented by this ticket before implementation follow-ups are created.
- The business `tenantId` claim and route policy remain separate from Microsoft Entra `tid`.

The current task-api only requires an authenticated user and the matching business tenant claim. Supporting both modes therefore requires a separately path-owned authorization follow-up, not only an actor extraction change.

## Decision and alternatives

Selected: typed subject plus immediate-client provenance.

Reasons:

- It supports human and workload actors without pretending every subject is a user.
- It distinguishes a direct delegated client from an OBO middle tier.
- It preserves the service principal for app-only and managed-identity calls.
- `tid` plus `oid` is stable across applications within an Entra tenant.
- `azp` or `appid` preserves which client exercised the subject's authority.
- A small shared actor-context module can hide token-version and flow differences from every endpoint.

Rejected: `sub` alone. It identifies the token subject, but it is pairwise to an application and does not preserve whether the subject is a user or workload or which client called task-api.

Rejected: caller-supplied body or custom-header attribution. Both values are caller-controlled unless a separately trusted intermediary strips and overwrites them. No such intermediary contract exists here.

Rejected: one field containing an asserted represented user. It loses the authenticated caller and enables impersonation unless representation is separately authorized.

Rejected: treating OBO as app-only. Microsoft defines OBO as delegated access that carries the user's identity through the request chain. App-only tokens cannot be exchanged through OBO.

Microsoft references:

- [Access token claims reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/access-token-claims-reference#payload-claims)
- [Validate token subjects and immutable identifiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/claims-validation#validate-the-subject)
- [Application-only access](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/app-only-access-primer)
- [On-behalf-of flow](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-on-behalf-of-flow)
- [Delegated and application permission claims](https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/entra/entra-id/app-integration/application-delegated-permission-access-tokens-identity-platform)
- [Configure JWT bearer authentication in ASP.NET Core](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/security/authentication/configure-jwt-bearer-authentication)

## Compatibility and migration

The event shape and tenant schema both change.

- New create and transition writes use the canonical typed actor identifier.
- `TaskTransitioned` retains its string `actor` field and adds `clientApplicationId` and `permissionMode`.
- `WorkflowTask.UpdatedBy` widens from `nvarchar(64)` to `nvarchar(128)`.
- Existing create records were token-derived, except that the current fallback can record `"unknown"`.
- Existing transition records and events may contain caller-supplied values. They are historical business labels, not proof of the authenticated principal.
- Historical records are not rewritten because the authenticated principal and immediate client cannot be reconstructed reliably after the request.
- New consumer models must define how replayed legacy events that lack the new fields are represented as `legacy-unverified`. They must not silently treat legacy actor text as authenticated provenance.
- Clients must remove `actor` from transition request bodies before adopting the revised contract.
- Follow-up tickets must define producer, contract, schema, and consumer rollout order before implementation starts.

## Blocked by

- [x] #40
- [x] #68

## Paths

- `docs/blueprint.md`
- `docs/decisions/ADR-001-transactional-outbox-with-cdc-relay.md`
- `docs/decisions/ADR-004-delta-events-with-version-numbers.md`
- `docs/specs/00-shared-contracts.md`
- `docs/specs/01-wire-format.md`
- `docs/specs/20-src-task-api.md`

`docs/specs/01-wire-format.md` was added to this list on 2026-08-28: the
`TaskTransitioned` event envelope (the `actor` field and the new
`clientApplicationId` and `permissionMode` fields) lives there, having moved out
of `00-shared-contracts.md`, and the Verification below requires the event
contract to be consistent. Overlap note: issue #190 (open, in-progress:s3) also
declares `docs/specs/01-wire-format.md` in its Paths, scoped to the signal-topic
and offset text near the end of the file; this ticket edits only the event
envelope near the top. The two edit regions are disjoint. A blocking edge was
added on 2026-08-28 (#190 is blocked by #172): #172 merges first and #190 rebases
its wire-format section onto the result, resolving any textual conflict then.

## Verification

Method: unit

Run `python3 scripts/ci/check_ascii.py docs` and `git diff --check`.

An independent Spec review must confirm that the blueprint, ADR-001, ADR-004, the shared HTTP and event contracts, and the task-api specification use the selected meanings consistently. The review must walk the four flow rows above and the legacy-event compatibility path.

## Acceptance checklist

- [ ] The current create-versus-transition provenance mismatch is stated plainly
- [ ] Delegated-user and application task writes are explicitly supported
- [ ] Direct delegated, OBO, client-credentials, and managed-identity flows are defined
- [ ] `actor`, user, workload, client application, and permission mode have unambiguous meanings
- [ ] Canonical `user:{tid}:{oid}` and `workload:{tid}:{oid}` actor identifiers are recorded
- [ ] `azp` and `appid` normalization into `clientApplicationId` is defined
- [ ] Delegated `scp` and application `roles` authorization are distinguished
- [ ] One task-write delegated scope and one task-write application role are named
- [ ] Missing token, invalid token, missing provenance claims, missing permissions, and tenant rejection have explicit HTTP outcomes
- [ ] Body and custom-header values cannot override provenance
- [ ] `WorkflowTask.UpdatedBy` width and semantics are defined
- [ ] `TaskTransitioned.actor`, `clientApplicationId`, and `permissionMode` are defined
- [ ] Create and transition use one shared actor-context interface
- [ ] The `"unknown"` create fallback is removed from the target behavior
- [ ] Tenant authorization remains separate from identity provenance and permission mode
- [ ] Async causation and support impersonation boundaries are stated
- [ ] Legacy task rows and events are explicitly marked unverified rather than reinterpreted
- [ ] Producer, shared-contract, schema, and consumer rollout order is documented
- [ ] Path-owned implementation follow-up tickets cover authorization configuration, task-api actor resolution, schema migration, shared contracts, consumer compatibility, and tests before this issue closes
- [ ] Follow-up tickets have explicit blocking edges and do not overlap paths
- [ ] No environment-specific tenant, client, object, or subject identifier is committed

## Out of scope

- Changing merged PR #171 or closed issue #40
- Implementing the selected model in application code or infrastructure
- Adding a general impersonation or delegation feature beyond validated OBO
- Adding asynchronous user-causation fields
- Adding an audit-ledger consumer, which is deferred from v1
- Redesigning the business `TenantRoute` policy
- Adding a new identity provider or token flow
- Reconstructing authenticated principals or clients for historical transitions

## Required implementation decomposition

Before this issue closes, create separately path-owned follow-up tickets for:

1. Exposing and configuring the delegated task-write scope and application task-write role.
2. Adding the shared actor-context module, permission checks, endpoint integration, and HTTP tests in task-api.
3. Widening `WorkflowTask.UpdatedBy` through the tenant-schema owner and proving upgrade behavior.
4. Extending `Lexfield.Contracts` and rolling the event changes through consumers with legacy-event tests.

The tickets must form an explicit blocking chain where their rollout order requires it.

## Size forecast

5 documentation files and at most 350 changed lines. Follow-up implementation work is forecast separately.

items.title: Demo epic: ontology → inventory/accounting app → jewelry specialization, with inherited guarantees

labels.name: epic
labels.description: Track or capability epic; checkpoint overview

items.body:
Checklist reconciled against GitHub on 2026-11-11.

**Goal (owner, 2026-11-01):** the AUC ES competition demo for #63. We define the business ontology, get a working small inventory/accounting application from those definitions, then specialize it for jewelry live without rebuilding the foundations.

## Demo script (what the audience sees)
1. **A working app.** Receive stock, transfer it, sell it, return it, then cancel or correct. Show the stock and the matching books.
2. **What built it.** Open the definitions (entities, relationships, actions, lifecycle and rules) and show how they drive the UI and the operations. The slice has no handwritten CRUD and no custom posting hooks.
3. **Add jewelry live.** Add purity, customer-owned metal and a refining operation with explicitly recorded loss. Run it and show its stock and ledger effects.
4. **Laws carry through.** Attempt a violating customization or transaction. It is refused with a readable reason, and no partial stock or ledger change survives.
5. **Evidence.** A Guarantees view lists each guarantee with its evidence level: proved on the model, enforced in execution, or tested for parity. ERPNext differential parity is supporting evidence.

Law stack: core primitives → accounting and inventory laws → jewelry laws (fine-metal conservation) → the tenant workflow.

## Scope
One ERPNext version, one company, one currency, FIFO plus moving average. ERPNext (GPL) is a black-box oracle: we reimplement from its behaviour and docs and never port its code.

## Units (each one merges independently, under 400 lines, through the normal merge bar)
- [ ] **Core laws:** #90 quantity, escrow and commitment laws; #91 workflows inherit the value laws; #94 inherited law origins in receipts
  - Status 2026-11-04: #94 merged. #90 and #91 are open and conflicting, stacked through #224 on #223, and #223 is on the hand-written-proof hold. The law re-cut train replaces this path: #828, #839 and #853 merged; #860–#864, #868 and #869 open.
- [ ] **Engine alpha** (alpha acceptance: author, registry, act via API/MCP/CLI with authz, ledger replay, read+subscribe parity, definition checks in CI): #141 #142 #143 #144 #147 #148 #149 #212
  - Status 2026-11-04: #143 and #144 merged. #141, #147, #148, #149 and #212 are open (mostly conflicting); #142 is on hold. Field-authority enforcement now continues in the Surfaces units (#884 in the queue, #831).
- [ ] **CI unblock:** #128 (#133, then #132), #127 / #145
  - Status 2026-11-04: #128 closed by #132; #133 and #145 merged. #127's fix #739 merged, and #127 stays open for the live post-landing confirmation.
- [ ] #214 stock core slice definitions
- [ ] #215 ERPNext differential parity harness on Boat
- [ ] #216 jewelry pack
- [ ] #217 refusal and Guarantees view (#177)
- [ ] #218 demo script and UI shell


## Demo beat 6: data engineering (owner, 2026-11-01; key audience: data scientists and engineers)
The same ontology is the semantic layer. Live: ERPNext and Shopify change feeds land in the REA layer through integration packs → a declared question ("inventory value by region and metal", "scrap yield by week") updates incrementally with a freshness label → click a number to drill down to its objects and the source documents (lineage) → a bad imported row becomes a quarantined **finding** with evidence, not a refusal → an as-of question before and after a restatement → a statistical analysis on the same data (forecast and regression from the norn-metrics work), with guarded publication. No pipeline code, SQL glue or separate BI tool. Acceptance: docs/spec/acceptance/data-engineering.md.

## Claims we will and won't make
We say "customizations preserve these named guarantees" and "no handwritten CRUD or posting hooks in this slice". We don't say "proven equivalent to ERPNext" or "no tests": the tests move into the parity and property harness.



## Plan (coordinator, updated 2026-11-01 ~01:20 UTC)
Owner directives: demo in ~4 days, significant progress by 2026-11-02; parallelise widely on Codex Sol; review is the CodeRabbit loop until nothing major, then the coordinator's mergeability read, then the merge queue; WellDB continues just below the demo in priority.

| Lane | Scope |

| a2: CI + core laws | #141, #133 → #132 (#128), #90 (split), #91, #94 |
