items.title: Add design patterns support —> 123-java-design-patterns
items.body:
# User Story: 123-java-design-patterns

**As a** Java developer using this cursor-rules-java project
**I want to** add a new `123-java-design-patterns` skill for Java design patterns support
**So that** I can get consistent, practical guidance for selecting, implementing, and refactoring toward appropriate design patterns in Java projects without over-engineering the codebase.

## Acceptance Criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Java design patterns skill

Background:
  Given the repository generates skills from XML sources under "skills-generator/src/main/resources"
  And generated content under "skills/" is not edited directly
  And the Java design guidance currently includes neighboring skills such as "121-java-object-oriented-design" and "122-java-type-design"

@acceptance-test
Scenario: Generate the Java design patterns skill from XML sources
  Given a new Java design patterns skill is defined in the skill generator sources
  When the skills-generator module is installed
  Then the generated skills include "123-java-design-patterns"
  And the skill explains when design patterns should and should not be applied
  And the skill provides practical Java examples for common creational, structural, and behavioral patterns
  And the skill emphasizes maintainability, simplicity, testability, and avoiding pattern overuse

@integration-test
Scenario: Register the Java design patterns skill in the skill catalog
  Given the Java design patterns skill XML source exists
  When the skill index and skill list are generated
  Then "123-java-design-patterns" appears in the generated skills inventory
  And the skill can be discovered with prompts such as "apply Java design patterns" or "refactor this code using an appropriate pattern"

@integration-test
Scenario: Align the new skill with existing Java design guidance
  Given the repository already contains object-oriented and type-design skills
  When the Java design patterns skill is authored
  Then it complements "121-java-object-oriented-design" and "122-java-type-design"
  And it avoids duplicating broad SOLID, type-design, and generic refactoring guidance that belongs in neighboring skills

@integration-test
Scenario: Keep generated artifacts reproducible
  Given the Java design patterns skill is generated from XML
  When "./mvnw clean verify -pl skills-generator" is executed
  Then the build succeeds
  And no generated skill content requires manual edits under "skills/"

@integration-test
Scenario: Validate generated skill quality
  Given the generated Java design patterns skill exists under "skills/"
  When "npx skill-check@latest skills --no-security-scan --format github" is executed
  Then the skill passes the formatter and structural checks
  And any behavioral scan findings are reviewed before promoting the change
```

## Notes

- Implement changes in XML sources under `skills-generator/src/main/resources/`, including the relevant skill reference, skill index, and catalog wiring.
- Do not edit generated `skills/` content directly; regenerate it through the Maven pipeline.
- Place the skill numerically between `122-java-type-design` and `124-java-secure-coding` as `123-java-design-patterns`.
- Cover the most useful Java design pattern families: creational, structural, and behavioral patterns.
- Include guidance for deciding whether a pattern is justified, with explicit warnings against pattern-driven design when simpler code is enough.
- Keep examples compatible with the repository guidance for Java 25 and Maven-based workflows.

## INVEST Validation

- **Independent**: The design patterns skill can be added as a new Java design skill without changing the behavior of existing OOP, type-design, or secure-coding skills.
- **Negotiable**: The exact set of patterns, examples, and anti-pattern warnings can be refined while preserving the intent of practical Java design-pattern guidance.
- **Valuable**: Java developers gain a focused skill for selecting and applying patterns thoughtfully, improving code structure while avoiding unnecessary complexity.
- **Estimable**: The work is bounded by creating and wiring one generated skill plus validation through the existing generator and skill-check workflows.
- **Small**: The scope should fit in one iteration because it follows the existing single-skill generation pattern.
- **Testable**: Completion can be verified by generated skill output, catalog discovery, Maven verification, and skill validation commands.

items.title: Split DBs by group + by DM (embedded replicas), keep shared directory DB
items.body:
> **Implementation-ready as of 2026-07-09.** Read in this order: (1) the [re-analysis comment](https://github.com/actuallydan/pollis/issues/261#issuecomment-4918590364) — current-arch audit, table split, platform status, phasing; (2) the [spec addendum](https://github.com/actuallydan/pollis/issues/261#issuecomment-4927184797) — envelope-GC/message-loss invariants, the `conversation_shard` backwards-compat state machine, failure-mode semantics, acceptance criteria. The body below is the original background; where they conflict, the comments win. Sequencing: after #515, after a Turso-Sync-Rust spike.

> **Update (2026-07-07):** The core premise "No server. We don't have one and don't want one" is no longer strictly true — the **Delivery Service** (`pollis-delivery`) now exists as the sole Turso writer (#419/#420). That materially changes the token-minting / provisioning analysis below: scoped per-DB token minting, DB provisioning, and member-removal token rotation can be **brokered through the DS** instead of baking an org-scoped Platform API token into the client binary. Re-read the "Constraints" and "What needs planning before we commit" sections against a DS-brokered model.

---

Follow-up to #259 (context merged below). Worth fleshing out later — needs planning before commit.

## Background (from #259 — Turso platform state, May 2026)

Turso has moved off regional/edge replicas. The two patterns they're pushing — **per-tenant DBs** and **Turso Sync** (true local-first with offline writes) — are partly available to us:

| Feature | Status | Rust SDK? |
|---|---|---|
| libSQL Embedded Replicas (`Builder::new_remote_replica`) | Legacy but supported. Reads local, writes remote. `offline: true` queues writes locally. | ✅ `libsql` crate (what we already use) |
| Turso Sync (new engine, true local-first) | Recommended for new projects. Logical-log push, physical-page pull. | ❌ Node + wasm only. Rust on roadmap, no ETA. |
| Offline writes (private beta) | `FAIL_ON_CONFLICT` / `DISCARD_LOCAL` / `REBASE_LOCAL` / `MANUAL_RESOLUTION` | ❌ Node only |
| Multi-DB Schemas (parent → child propagation) | **Deprecated for new users.** Each DB self-migrates. | n/a |
| Edge/regional replicas | Deprecated for new users. | n/a |
| Platform API for DB provisioning | Live: `POST /v1/organizations/{org}/databases`, supports `seed` | bearer-token HTTP, callable from Rust |

**Implication for Rust desktop in 2026:** Embedded Replicas is the only first-class sync surface. Anything per-DB has to come through that, plus the Platform API for provisioning.

### Constraints

- **No server.** We don't have one and don't want one. Rules out the textbook per-tenant flow ("backend mints a scoped token at signup"). Org-scoped Platform API tokens baked into the binary are hostile-user-unsafe; we already ship a descoped one without schema perms and need to verify create-only scoping for this plan.
- **Messaging is cross-user.** `send_message`, `search_user_by_username`, MLS key package fetch, membership queries — none of those work in a strict per-user split. A shared *directory* DB has to survive in any per-tenant design.

### Why per-group + per-DM over the alternatives in #259

#259 walked through four options:
- **A. Embedded Replica of the shared DB.** ~20 LOC, big read-latency win, but doesn't fix the shared-token smell or scale crypto/data boundaries.
- **B. A + `offline: true`.** Adds offline writes; conflict model needs design; still one DB / one token.
- **C. Hybrid: per-user DB for private state, shared DB stays the bus.** Unlocks multi-device for drafts/cursors/MLS state. Requires provisioning. Still serialises all message envelopes through one DB.
- **D. Per-channel DB.** Cleanest MLS alignment, but per-channel granularity is too fine (groups can have many channels), and Multi-DB Schemas being deprecated makes hand-managing schemas across that many DBs painful.

This plan is **D at group/DM granularity** — coarse enough that schema fan-out is manageable, fine enough that the crypto/data boundary matches membership. It also subsumes C: per-group replica is the natural home for MLS group state, which currently lives in local SQLite.

## Shape

- **Shared directory DB** (today's Turso, slimmed down): `users`, `user_groups`, `user_dms`, invites, public keys / MLS key packages. Tells each client which group/DM DBs to open.
- **Per-group DB** (one embedded replica per group): channels, group membership, message envelopes, MLS group state.
- **Per-DM DB** (one embedded replica per DM): same shape, 2 members.

Frontend doesn't know — `invoke("send_message", { channelId })` still works, routing happens inside the Tauri command.

## Why it's appealing

- Crypto boundary = data boundary. Non-members literally don't hold a token for the DB.
- Reads become local-microsecond. Big sidebar / channel-switch win.
- No cross-group index contention. A 50k-message group doesn't slow down anyone else's queries.
- Per-group sync granularity — quiet groups cost nothing, active group syncs hot.

## What needs planning before we commit

1. **Provisioning.** `create_group` and first-DM send need to create new Turso DBs via Platform API. Confirmed Turso supports descoped tokens (we already ship one without schema perms) — need to verify a create-DBs-but-not-delete-others scoping is achievable so we can bake it into the binary instead of standing up a Worker.
2. **Replica lifecycle.** Power user in 50 groups + 100 DMs = 150 replicas. Need lazy-open on channel select, LRU eviction (probably cap ~30 open), token cache. fd budget is real — we hit "too many open files" with one DB (#244).
3. **Sync cadence.** 150 replicas on a poll interval = 150× request rate. Foregrounded replica syncs aggressively, background replicas on long interval. Logic we have to write.
4. **In-app schema migrator.** Multi-DB Schemas is deprecated. Each replica self-migrates on first open after app upgrade using a `schema_migrations` table + binary-embedded migration list (we already have this pattern in `pollis-core/src/db/mod.rs`). Idempotent under concurrent open, advisory lock via `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Migrations remain additive-and-backward-compatible (already our rule) because two members on different app versions share the DB.
5. **Member removal / token rotation.** Removing a member means revoking their token to that group's DB. Cleanest is rotating the DB's token and re-issuing to remaining members — need to understand Turso's rotation primitives and how heavy this is at the group-churn rate.
6. **Cross-DB queries we currently take for granted.** Sidebar unread counts fan out to N replicas. Fast locally but new code.
7. **DM bootstrap handoff.** Alice provisions a new DB for the DM, has to deliver Bob's scoped token through the shared directory (`pending_dm_invites` keyed to Bob's pubkey, token encrypted to his MLS key package). Needs spam gating.

## Rough sizing (ignoring schema split)

- `ReplicaPool` (lazy open, LRU eviction, token cache): ~300 LOC
- Re-point commands in `pollis-core/src/commands/{messages,channels,groups,mls}.rs` to route by group_id: ~400-600 LOC touched, mechanical
- Platform API client for provisioning + token mint: ~150 LOC
- In-app migrator: ~100 LOC
- `remote.rs` new replica-mode constructor: ~50 LOC

Net ~1000-1500 LOC new + mechanical re-pointing. Frontend ~zero change. Hard part is lifecycle correctness (sync failures, token refresh, member-removal rotation), not LOC.

## Performance expectations

- Reads: large win (microseconds vs ~50ms hrana roundtrip).
- Writes: roughly unchanged (still hit per-replica remote, sync back).
- Cold start: lazy-open trades fast boot for a one-shot sync delay on first channel select per session. Probably prefetch on sidebar hover.

## Open questions before scoping

- Exact Turso token scoping primitives (create-only, rotation cost, time-bounded).
- Does Turso issue **append-only / write-only** per-DB tokens? Would simplify DM bootstrap and key-package writes (from #259).
- Replica fd / memory cost in practice — needs a load test before we commit.
- `replica.db` disk-size growth for an active user over months — bounds replica-pool cost (from #259).
- Does `libsql::Database::sync()` cleanly handle the stream-tore-down cases that motivated `RemoteDb::reconnect()` (#247)? (from #259)
- Any movement on a Rust `@tursodatabase/sync` equivalent? If < 6 months out, waiting beats migrating twice (from #259).
- Whether MLS group state moves into the per-group replica or stays in local SQLite. Moving it would give multi-device the MLS state it needs, which #259 Option C also flagged.

## References

- Turso Sync intro: https://turso.tech/blog/introducing-databases-anywhere-with-turso-sync
- Offline writes (private beta): https://turso.tech/blog/introducing-offline-writes-for-turso
- Embedded Replicas (legacy): https://docs.turso.tech/features/embedded-replicas/introduction
- Platform API `databases.create`: https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/create
- Multi-DB Schemas (deprecated): https://docs.turso.tech/features/multi-db-schemas
- Roadmap context (edge replicas deprecation): https://turso.tech/blog/upcoming-changes-to-the-turso-platform-and-roadmap
- Per-user DB walkthrough: https://turso.tech/blog/give-each-of-your-users-their-own-sqlite-database-b74445f4

items.title: Program: Elsa 4 unified execution foundation
items.body:
[Codex] On behalf of @sfmskywalker.

# Elsa 4 unified execution program

Status: **In Progress — owner-approved SQLite native/BPMN milestone resumed (8 November 2026).** The active scope and finish line below supersede the prior ETL-first work order for this delivery increment. The wider program remains open.
Product owner: Sipke Schoorstra. Steward: the active program lead, with one shared leaf queue and one integration lane.
Date: 2026-10-17. Canonical remote status: [Program #2892](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/2892).

## Active delivery milestone — 8 November 2026

Owner-approved resumption: **Recoverable native/BPMN composition on SQLite**. Codex continues the existing program autonomously within this smaller scope; completing it does not complete Program #2892.

> Deliver a verified SQLite execution milestone in which a native workflow invokes BPMN, waits durably, survives host restart, and handles completion, fault, retry and cancellation correctly. Preserve model-specific semantics and existing authoring contracts. Reuse merged recovery evidence, close the remaining gaps, remove demonstrated obsolete code and redundant tests, and verify the integrated result on main.

### Finish line

- SQLite, built-in host, root native parent, and existing supported BPMN human/service-task paths. No new model-neutral kernel is a prerequisite.
- Reuse merged #3988 publication/GC classification, #3992 pending-parent-result crash, #3993 held retry/fault and #3995 composite-child crash evidence at their declared revisions. They are not blanket current-main/platform/Studio acceptance.
- Verify cancellation while waiting and refusal of late results after cancellation on the selected composition. Retain unique recovery, authority, compatibility and cancellation coverage.
- Disposition the recorded #3993 post-restart timeout causally; later passes alone do not explain it. Complete applicable authoring/API compatibility checks.
- Remove obsolete paths and genuinely redundant tests only where coverage remains. Record persistence/coordination overhead for this journey without expanding into the performance program.
- Deliver a runnable example and supported-profile/limitations documentation; independent review, green exact-head required checks, protected landing and resulting-main verification remain required.

### Deferred from this milestone, retained in the program

R3 managed-store recovery, ETL expansion, native collaboration, additional providers, multi-host qualification, comprehensive Studio/browser acceptance and generic-kernel extraction. Existing claims, holds, review counts and failed/unrun evidence are preserved. This resumption does not restart their paused workers or automations; other programs retain separate ownership.

### Current checkpoint

Starting main: `49c10b7732506a708f7cafa6932768c9b9556c13`. No new runtime pass or completion claim. First active increment is the selected-path cancellation/late-result coverage audit and analysis of the recorded restart timeout, followed by targeted verification and only demonstrated corrections. Project #62 intended status remains In Progress. The Codex App currently cannot resolve org Project #62; program comments are the explicit board-checkpoint fallback until access is restored.

## Broader program goal — retained from 29 October 2026

> Deliver Elsa’s execution-model program #2892 end to end through working, recoverable user journeys across BPMN, native workflows, ETL and Studio. Preserve existing authoring and persisted-state compatibility. Let demonstrated journey needs drive architecture, deliver small verified increments, and keep the issues, PRs and Project #62 current.

[Owner confirmation](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/2892#issuecomment-6489393346). The #2898 / PR #3410 lane is completed and successor PR #3603 is merged. Continue the existing #2908 ETL lane through runtime-provider concurrency and real-host qualification, #3789, transform chains/admission, recovery/stale-writer proofs and BPMN/Studio acceptance. Broader #2907, #2905 and agent/program obligations remain open; retain existing compatibility safeguards and deferrals.

## Approved production continuation — 18 October 2026

Sipke instructed implementation of the full remaining program. [Approved delivery scope and ordered milestones](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/2892#issuecomment-6249319967) supersede the earlier research-only readiness gate below. [BPMN library authority](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/2892#issuecomment-6249325156) additionally authorizes necessary library changes and releases, with review and compatibility gates.

Confirmed scope, reconciled with the [20 October owner reprioritization](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/2892#issuecomment-6287993256): native/BPMN shared production lifecycle; qualified built-in hosting with further Orleans qualification explicitly deferred; independent fourth-model package; all four ETL connector families with PostgreSQL and SQL Server; production native agent composition; integrated Studio; verified HTML. BPMN arbitrary alteration, live-instance migration and a full operator console are deferred. Agent completion uses deterministic and provider-protocol tests; live model tests are opt-in. External effects remain at least once. No unrelated releases or deployments are authorized.

Lifecycle compatibility leaf #2960 is complete. BPMN PRs #51 and #57 are merged following exact-head Code Review approval, with post-merge package/test/wiki evidence recorded below. Native runtime leaf #2967 is merged in PR #2970; exact-merge verification is complete; #2735 still requires the released upstream prerequisites. The completed #2914 proof and its CI limitations remain unchanged.

## Vision and users

Elsa 4 is the workflow engine and BPMN engine for .NET, with a foundation that can later support a first-class ETL engine. Developers author and extend executable behavior; operators recover and inspect executions; process participants complete human work; integration authors connect systems. They share a coherent platform without forcing every semantic model into one graph or interpreter.

Optimize for correctness, architectural fit, clear responsibility and extensibility. Existing frameworks and custom implementations are alternatives to evaluate, not commitments justified by familiarity or AI-assisted implementation cost.

## Agreed direction and boundaries

1. One durable execution foundation; multiple semantic engines and extensible composition components.
2. Flowchart owns joins, Sequence owns ordering, StateMachine owns transitions. Shared runtime mechanisms do not reinterpret those rules or infer parent completion merely because child jobs ended.
3. A workflow/process instance is the virtual-actor coordination boundary. Activities and composites do not become individual actors. A pipeline execution may have an addressable coordinator; independently leased partition workers need not be actors.
4. Distinguish semantic scope, state ownership, actor activation and computational work. One orchestration owner can coordinate many concurrent workers.
5. Actor hosting is pluggable. Preserve ADR 0078: one membership view, capability-aware placement, authoritative commit fencing and durable owed-work tracking. Orleans is the first adapter experiment, not a selected default.
6. Background activity execution and ETL partitions should share only demonstrated durable dispatch/recovery mechanisms. Activity authoring remains independent of actor-framework APIs. Offloading does not change Sequence/Flowchart semantics.
7. Activities eligible for offloading need explicit invocation identity, pinned implementation, isolated inputs/context and correlated outputs/effects. Live mutable coordinator context must not escape to workers. Business errors, technical failures and incidents remain distinct.
8. BPMN is first-class. Direct BPMN hosting and the BpmnProcess embedding adapter use the same semantics implementation. Preserve existing frozen contracts and adopt #2735's library work rather than creating a second token engine.
9. ETL target: native .NET; finite batches and continuous event integration; distributed partitions with a local transform chain; bounded batches/backpressure; mappings, filtering, validation, routing and lookups. Files, HTTP, SQL and RabbitMQ are initial connector candidates. Defer cross-worker individual stages, windows/stream joins and general analytics.
10. At-least-once execution with explicit idempotency and external-effect recovery. No universal exactly-once side-effect claim.
11. Design/runtime separation, immutable pinned artifacts, tenant/authority propagation, versioned state, recovery and observable operational outcomes are requirements.
12. Human tasks, incident tools, alterations, migration and analytics are surrounding modules. Identify their foundation contracts now; do not implement the whole product in this program's evidence milestone.
13. Interactive HTML follows evidence. It communicates the architecture and its limits; visual polish is not proof.

These are owner-approved directions from this conversation, not newly ratified public interfaces or replacements for accepted ADRs. Where the evidence implies changing an accepted contract, obtain a reviewed ADR amendment before production work.

## Primary journeys and success criteria

- A native workflow schedules independent background activities concurrently, preserves sequential composition, persists outcomes and resumes after a crash without losing or repeating logical continuation.
- A BPMN process runs directly and through BpmnProcess with equivalent normalized semantic traces: fork/join, restart, human wait, interrupting timer, late result, worker incident and a narrowly validated alteration.
- A workflow or BPMN service task invokes a distributed pipeline. Partitions progress independently; a worker dies after external delivery but before checkpoint; recovery uses destination idempotency and refuses stale progress. Parent success, fault and cancellation map explicitly.
- The built-in host satisfies its declared conformance requirements without changing definitions or activity code. Real third-party provider qualification remains tracked but owner-deferred under the 20 October reprioritization; it is not passed, and Proto.Actor has not been selected.
- A separate package adds a fourth semantic model without new model-specific branches in the common substrate; unsupported capabilities are refused clearly.
- An operator can inspect durable work, incidents and causal history through supported boundaries. A browser reader can explore the evidence-backed architecture through the later HTML artifact.

## Source evidence and its limits

The existing report `docs/reports/unified-execution-three-case-proof.md` and prototype at `tools/experiments/UnifiedExecution.Prototype/` are historical evidence at local commit `4cc63596d`: 115 assertions, 68 worker processes and three negative mutations, with 622 architecture tests and map checks reported. These are prior results, not newly run gates or multi-host proof. Lease time was logical, not a real distributed clock experiment. The prototype does not prove BPMN conformance, framework substitution, general commit replay, complete cancellation or plugin registration.

Historical source-audit note: the then-local checkout predated the source-layout consolidation visible in issue #2501 (Essentials/, Extensions/, Studio/). Before implementation refresh upstream refs, current paths, ownership, claims and exact-head checks. Never copy stale source paths into a new implementation task without resolving them.

Relevant sources: local actor/placement/checkpoint implementations; Elsa 3 background middleware and invoker inspected at be5bdae50; actual Bpmn.Semantics integration owned by #2735; ADRs 0031, 0063, 0073 and 0078. Camunda worker/task/modification/migration documentation informs capability boundaries, not a compatibility promise.

## Roadmap and gates

| Milestone | Outcome | Exit evidence |
|---|---|---|
| M0: durable control room | Plan, decisions, native issue hierarchy, next leaf and recovery instructions survive context loss | Read-back of issue bodies, hierarchy and dependencies; local committed plan; board limitation explicit |
| M1: evidence and falsification | Realistic witnesses challenge the proposed shared boundaries | Baseline reconciliation; activity/partition work proof; actual BPMN operational witness; real actor-provider substitution; independently added semantic module |
| M2: architecture decision | Smallest justified contracts and migration strategy | Reviewed decision packet records alternatives, failed assumptions, capability requirements, affected contracts and explicit accept/revise/reject outcomes |
| M3: production vertical slices | Native workflow and BPMN journeys run through adopted mechanisms | Approved specs, narrow implementation PRs, existing compatibility checks plus affected end-to-end failure/recovery proofs |
| M4: ETL delivery | Distributed batch and continuous ingestion journeys with initial connectors | Real connector failure/replay/acknowledgement evidence and declared limits; no universal exactly-once claim |
| Communication after M2 | Interactive architecture explainer | Source-linked claims, current evidence labels, accessible zoom/drill-down and scenario playback; browser QA |

M1 order: baseline -> shared work witness -> provider witness. BPMN evidence can proceed independently after baseline once #2735's selected library/parity prerequisites are satisfied. The independent extension witness follows shared work, BPMN and provider evidence. M2 follows all witnesses. HTML follows M2 and does not wait for all production delivery. Later feature tasks are progressively elaborated; no speculative production leaf backlog is ready today.

## Historical research gate and deferred decisions

The original M0/M1 gate below is historical; the 18 October continuation above authorizes production delivery. At that original checkpoint, the gate passed only for M0/M1 planning and bounded research. The mission, users, semantic boundaries, native .NET preference, distributed recovery requirement and evidence acceptance criteria are settled. No production implementation task is ready by this decision.

| Open decision | Owner and revisit trigger | Why safely deferred |
|---|---|---|
| Exact shared contracts, ownership keys and work schemas | Program lead recommends; Sipke/architecture reviewers decide at M2 | M1 tests candidates without freezing production APIs |
| Orleans versus built-in default; Proto.Actor follow-up | Sipke at M2 after provider witness | One adapter proves a seam without selecting the production default |
| Full supported BPMN execution profile | Existing BPMN owner before release claims | Hosting witness is explicitly narrower; unsupported constructs must be diagnosed |
| #2735 library version, upstream fixes and resumption timing | Codex owns the existing three-PR adoption stack under Sipke’s [25 October transfer](https://github.com/elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation/issues/2735#issuecomment-6396983746) | Prior owner reservation is superseded; continue exact claim6396984230 and PR3335. The library0.5.0/payload1.10.0 is the parity target, not completed Foundation adoption. |
| Hosting topology, connector-specific transaction/security policies | Feature owner before relevant production task is Ready | Evidence harness is isolated and makes no production guarantee |
| Release compatibility, rollout and publisher/operations ownership | Existing #2501/#1970/#2092 owners plus Sipke before M3 | Program changes no release policy or deployment now |
| Commercial entitlement and human-task UX scope | Sipke before corresponding product feature | M1 uses a minimal task harness, no entitlement policy |

## Repository and existing-program ownership

- `elsa-workflows/elsa-foundation` owns this program's coordination and future shared execution work. Resolve current monorepo paths under #2501 before implementation; optional integrations follow the approved extension layout.
- `valence-works/bpmn` owns reusable BPMN semantics. Foundation #2735 owns its Elsa 4 adoption/parity. Link upstream dependencies; do not duplicate or reparent existing work.
- Existing BPMN Engine, Runtime Execution Seam, Runtime Alterations and Runtime Execution Evidence buckets retain their current scopes. In particular Execution Evidence is a product capability, not this research ledger.
- Foundation #2771 retains Elsa 3/4 parity ownership; #2747 incident retry and #1307 pump concurrency are related findings to reconcile, not automatically absorbed tasks.
- #2501 and #1970 retain repository/release topology. This program does not rename repositories or assume local historical paths are current.

## Evidence requirements

Every witness records exact source/library/provider versions, commands, fixtures, observable outcomes, negative controls, raw durable artifacts where safe, untested boundaries and an independent review. Test duplicate and conflicting receipts; crash before dispatch and after external effect; expiry and stale writers; cancellation versus late success; early versus late completion; fault versus business error; tenant/authority isolation and incompatible version placement where the witness crosses those boundaries. Logical-clock and single-machine evidence must remain labelled as such; the provider witness must include real multi-process cluster behavior and state its network-failure coverage.

Do not use scheduler work-count, issue closure or an animation as a success proxy. No throughput claims or reinstatement of retired benchmark gates. Production changes later use the normal Speckit/constitution/e2e and review gates for the affected scope.

## Interactive HTML presentation brief

Deliver after M2 evidence review, as a self-contained HTML artifact with a usable offline fallback. Provide overview, semantic composition, execution-instance/actor, worker/dataflow and recovery views. Support pan/zoom, drill-down, breadcrumbs, a legend and accessible keyboard navigation. Scenario controls cover normal execution, crash/reclaim, duplicate result and cancellation races. Distinguish a visualization/simulation from a live engine trace. Link every asserted guarantee to its evidence and mark proposed/unsupported behavior. Show workflow instance as the actor boundary, not every node; show ETL records bypassing the coordinator. Include source links, evidence revision/date, reduced-motion support and a concise presenter path. Use 3D only if it improves comprehension. Do not build or publish it before the evidence gate.

## Continuity protocol

GitHub issues are the authoritative progress/ownership record. This document owns product intent and staged acceptance; accepted ADRs own architecture gates; reports own findings; specs own approved work-unit details. The program-goal file is the repository entrypoint, not a competing task board.

On every resume: read the program issue and latest checkpoint; read this plan and the existing proof report; refresh all relevant issue/PR/dependency/claim state; resolve current source topology; identify the single active leaf or next eligible leaf. Read the leaf acceptance criteria and required evidence before touching code. Never infer that a closed issue, an old green check or a prior chat means current proof passed.

At each material transition: update the leaf issue with exact branch/commit, evidence, next action and blocker; reconcile parent acceptance and ready state; update the program's compact status table. Release issue claims explicitly. Checkpoint before context compaction or handoff. One active leaf by default; independent research can be delegated read-only. Keep future production features out of the worker queue until their requirements gate passes.

A checkpoint contains: current milestone; active/next issue; branch/worktree and exact SHA; last verified evidence; blockers and decision owners; next concrete command/action; things not yet proved. Durable evidence must be committed or embedded/uploaded to GitHub, not exist only in /tmp or chat. If a required document is only local, attach its content to the program issue until a normal documentation PR makes it available remotely.

## Project board

[Elsa 4 Unified Execution Foundation — Project #62](https://github.com/orgs/elsa-workflows/projects/62) is operational as of 2026-10-19 after the owner completed the installation permission update. A fresh App token confirmed organization and repository Projects administration. The App created the board and independently read back the initial 27 items (26 hierarchy issues plus PR #3077), 165 field values and six views: Roadmap, Execution, Critical Path, Agent Queue, Workstreams and Blocked. Status and Verification are separate; research proof closure does not imply production qualification. GitHub issues, native parentage/dependencies and evidence receipts remain authoritative.

The board is currently private. The App can administer items/fields/views, but GitHub rejected changing its visibility. No personal-account fallback or permission bypass was used. The original 2026-10-17 creation denial is resolved; visibility is the remaining narrow limitation. This board creates no automation or recurring execution.

items.title: Quant Ecosystem War Room — canonical command, tasks, approvals & evidence
items.body:
# Quant Ecosystem War Room — Canonical Control Plane

This issue (#902) is the **single coordination/control plane** for all active Quant Ecosystem agents, coordinators, reviewers, and deployment lanes.

**Room owner:** User/CEO  
**Lead coordinator:** GPT-5.6 Sol (coordination, source audit, architecture review, repo-work approvals within granted access)  
**Execution rule:** PR-only. No direct main mutation. Merge only through the repository/pipeline policy.

> Important authority boundary: agents should request normal engineering/workflow approval here from the lead coordinator. **Only the real user can approve credential sharing, secrets, billing/spend, account ownership/permission changes, production-destructive actions, legal/financial commitments, or other irreversible/high-impact external actions.** The coordinator must escalate those; it must never impersonate the user.

---

## 1. Single-command-center rule

1. Before starting a task, every lane reads the latest #902 checkpoint and its own open task.
2. Work instructions, ownership, conflicts, approvals, blockers, evidence, and completion reports are recorded here.
3. Do not treat side-channel instructions as canonical if they conflict with #902. Bring the conflict here and stop the conflicting action.
4. No agent may silently change another lane's branch, ownership, architecture contract, or deployment.
5. Every agent must report facts with evidence. “Done”, “fixed”, “works”, or “deployed” without proof is not accepted.
6. Check this room at each meaningful task transition and approximately every ~5 minutes while actively working when the runtime permits it.

---

## 2. Authority and approval model

### A — No extra approval required
Read-only audit, source inspection, tests, local reproduction, screenshots, competitor research, documentation, and drafting a proposed patch.

### B — Lead-coordinator approval in #902
Creating/altering a working branch, opening/updating a PR, choosing between conflicting implementation approaches, changing shared contracts/tokens/registries, requesting another lane's integration work, or moving a task from REVIEW to VERIFY.

Use:
`APPROVAL REQUEST | taskId | action | why | files/services | risk | rollback | evidence`

Coordinator answers:
`APPROVED` / `APPROVED WITH CONDITIONS` / `CHANGES REQUIRED` / `ESCALATE TO USER`.

### C — Explicit real-user approval required
Credentials/test-identity sharing across agents/accounts; secrets; billing/spend; cloud/account ownership or permissions; production-destructive changes; deleting data/resources; externally binding/legal/financial actions; or anything the connected system itself requires the account owner to approve.

**Never paste credentials, tokens, secrets, or private keys into this issue.** Use the proper secure channel/tool when authorized.

---

## 3. Task ledger — mandatory format

Every piece of work gets one task card:

```
TASK <taskId>
lane/owner:
goal:
app/service:
branch/PR:
dependencies:
acceptance tests:
evidence required:
risk/approval tier:
status:
blocker:
next action:
```

Recommended IDs: `WR-MAIL-###`, `WR-CHAT-###`, `WR-AI-###`, `WR-SSO-###`, `WR-INFRA-###`, `WR-UX-###`, `WR-REVIEW-###`.

Statuses are only:
`BACKLOG -> READY -> IN_PROGRESS -> BLOCKED -> REVIEW -> VERIFY -> DONE`

A task can move to **DONE** only when its acceptance evidence exists.

---

## 4. Evidence gates

### Code change
Exact file/finding + commit/PR + relevant tests/CI.

### UI/UX screen
`screen | route | auth state | desktop evidence | 390px/mobile evidence | loading | empty | error | keyboard/focus | gap/PR | state`

Missing evidence = **PENDING**, never PASS.

### Deployment
Deployed build/commit SHA + environment + replica/image consistency where applicable + live probe/journey.

### Cross-app action
Owner-product receipt/resource ID + verification + task/correlation ID + deployed SHA + live journey evidence.

**Code review alone cannot mark an interconnected journey PASS.**

---

## 5. Shared ecosystem architecture contract

All lanes follow the current Interconnection Plan v1 unless a conflict is raised here with source evidence:

- one identity, many apps;
- owner product mutates its own resources;
- one canonical app/capability registry;
- one durable task model;
- receipts/verification, not toast-only “success”;
- permissions are separate from SSO;
- cross-app handoff preserves source, target, `returnTo`, task/node and resource context;
- durable idempotency/task/receipt storage for multi-pod/restart safety;
- no production use of fake/in-memory URL-only pipelines.

Conflicting code must be reported before implementation proceeds.

---

## 6. Unified UI/UX acceptance bar

Target: a professional, dark-first connected product family — consistent structure/behavior, app-specific locked accent/logo.

Shared surfaces:
- app switcher;
- Quant Account/account switcher;
- persistent Quanty entry/task bar;
- task timeline + approvals;
- notification/receipt drawer;
- back-to-origin/cross-app breadcrumb;
- offline/error/retry/partial/unknown states;
- command palette/global shortcuts;
- permission/approval sheet.

Acceptance requires desktop + mobile evidence where tooling permits. Tooling gaps must be stated honestly; do not fabricate mobile/authenticated proof.

---

## 7. Required agent update format

At start:
`START | taskId | owner | branch | goal | dependencies | ETA not required`

During work only when meaningful:
`UPDATE | taskId | finding/change | evidence | blocker | next`

If blocked:
`BLOCKED | taskId | exact blocker | who/what can unblock | safe work continuing`

For review:
`REVIEW READY | taskId | PR/commit | tests | risks | evidence`

For completion:
`DONE | taskId | PR/commit | CI | deployed SHA if applicable | live evidence/receipt | remaining gaps`

No ACK-only messages when evidence or a decision is due.

---

## 8. Conflict protocol

If two agents touch the same contract/files/journey:
1. stop overlapping mutation;
2. post both approaches here with source evidence;
3. lead coordinator chooses or requests changes;
4. only then resume;
5. no cross-branch cherry-pick/merge without explicit coordination.

---

## 9. Current lane ownership

- **MUSE-ORCHESTRATOR / QuantMail + Identity:** Mail/Calendar/Drive/Contacts capability mapping, Quant Account/SSO, UI evidence.
- **Muse / QuantChat:** chat capabilities, receipts, deep links, E2EE/permission boundaries, UI coverage.
- **COPPER-TIGER / QuantAI:** planner/orchestrator consumer, route/capability reconciliation, QuantAI UI and live evidence.
- **Deploy/Infra:** durable task/idempotency/receipt topology, rollout, build/SHA/replica proof.
- **CODEX-REVIEW:** architecture/security conflict review against main/open PRs.
- **GPT-5.6 Sol:** lead coordination + independent source audit + shared architecture/contract review + targeted repo fixes.

Lane owners must expose gaps; unknown = PENDING, not PASS.

---

## 10. Current flagship acceptance journeys

A. Mail + Calendar + optional Chat meeting with retry without duplicate side effects.  
B. Drive file -> QuantAI -> saved artifact -> Mail/Chat, with version/resource receipts and revocation handling.  
C. Protected deep link -> login/account chooser -> exact destination, account switch, logout/session revocation.  
D. Quanty action visible across apps, resumable after browser reopen, with cancel/undo/retry where supported.

These are the proof journeys before broad “ecosystem connected” claims.

---

## 11. User escalation format

When only the real user can decide, post:

```
USER DECISION REQUIRED
taskId:
decision:
why required:
options:
risk of each:
recommended option:
what stays blocked:
```

Continue all independent safe work while waiting. Do not repeatedly ask for the same approval once the user has answered.

---

## 12. Standing rules

- No fake success.
- No secrets in comments.
- No direct-main work.
- No destructive production changes without real-user approval.
- No duplicated PRs without checking existing work.
- No “PASS” without the relevant evidence gate.
- Keep #902 as the canonical command, task, approval, blocker, and evidence record.

Latest dynamic status belongs in checkpoint comments below; this issue body is the stable operating contract.

---

## 13. Shared learning memory — mistakes must improve the system

#902 is also the **durable shared operational memory** for all agents. Do not rely on private model memory, local notes, or side-channel context as the only place a lesson exists.

### Mandatory learning loop

Before starting a task:
1. read the task's latest checkpoint;
2. scan relevant `LESSON` entries for the same app/contract/file/journey;
3. state which prior lessons apply in the `START` message;
4. convert those lessons into explicit acceptance checks before coding.

Whenever a mistake, failed assumption, stale report, failed test, security flaw, duplicate effort, or rework occurs, post:

```
LESSON <lessonId>
taskId:
app/lane:
trigger:
wrong assumption/action:
root cause:
how detected:
correction:
new guardrail/test:
files/contracts affected:
applies to other lanes:
evidence:
```

A lesson is not complete until it creates a reusable guardrail: a test, checklist item, schema/contract rule, lint/static check, runbook change, evidence gate, or ownership rule.

### Learning categories

Use one or more:
`STATUS_TRUTH` · `CONTRACT_DRIFT` · `SECURITY` · `EVIDENCE_GAP` · `DUPLICATE_WORK` · `DEPLOYMENT` · `UI_PARITY` · `NATIVE_PARITY` · `AUTH` · `IDEMPOTENCY` · `OBSERVABILITY`.

### Peer sharing rule

When a lesson can affect another lane, the discovering agent posts:

`SHARE | lessonId | from lane | affected lanes | exact risk | required check`

Affected lanes must reply with either:
- `APPLIED | lessonId | taskId | guardrail/test added | evidence`
- `NOT_APPLICABLE | lessonId | source-backed reason`

No ACK-only response.

### Permission memory

All engineering/workflow permission requests remain in #902:
`APPROVAL REQUEST | taskId | action | why | files/services | risk | rollback | evidence`

Approval decisions must reference the task and remain in this room so future agents can see **what was allowed, why, and under what conditions**.

User-only actions still use `USER DECISION REQUIRED` and must never be inferred from an old or unrelated approval.

### Post-task reflection

Every `DONE` or `VERIFY` transition includes:
`LEARNING | what surprised us | what nearly failed | guardrail added | lesson IDs reused/created`

If nothing was learned, explicitly say `LEARNING | no new lesson; prior lessons applied: <ids>`.

### Coordinator responsibility

The lead coordinator periodically:
- deduplicates repeated lessons;
- promotes recurring lessons into the stable issue-body rules;
- flags contradictory lessons/contracts;
- assigns owners to convert lessons into tests/automation;
- rejects “fixed” claims when the root cause is not prevented from recurring.

The goal is not zero mistakes; the goal is **no repeated preventable mistake**.

items.title: tubafrenzy turndown data-finalization (BS side): final-dump one-shot sweeps + preservation

labels.name: tubafrenzy
labels.description: Touches WXYC/tubafrenzy (webhook, legacy mirror, flowsheet ETL, reconcile)

labels.name: status:blocked
labels.description: Cannot start until a dependency closes

labels.name: deadline:tubafrenzy-turndown
labels.description: Hard clock: must land before the 2026-08-31 tubafrenzy turndown

labels.name: sev:med
labels.description: Triage severity: impact under common conditions

items.body:
## Problem

tubafrenzy is decommissioned 2026-09-07 (org Project #36; [WXYC/wiki#86](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/86) Phase-0 decision log). Several open Backend-Service issues describe data conditions whose *mechanism* dies during turndown (mirror, inbound webhooks, and the flowsheet + rotation ETLs all at **Phase 3** — [wiki#88](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/88), whose ETL stop is prepped in [#1858](https://github.com/WXYC/Backend-Service/pull/1858); `library-etl` alone at **Phase 3.5** — [wiki#89](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/89), which is chain-ready-gated with no calendar date, unlike Phase 3's committed 2026-09-07. The three ETLs do **not** stop together, and none of them is gated on Phase 5: [wiki#92](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/92) is dev/test-infra and script cleanup, not an ETL shutoff) but whose *residue* becomes permanent the moment there is no authoritative upstream to reconcile against. Once MySQL is gone, the only authoritative record of the legacy state is the final `mysqldump` captured at last-write. This ticket is the single consumer of that dump on the Backend-Service side: every one-shot cleanup, repair, and preservation task that keys on it lands here rather than as a standing mechanism nobody will maintain for a pipe with weeks to live.

## Blocked by

Native-blocked on the **final `mysqldump` capture** — a [wiki#86](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/86) / Phase-6 deliverable, re-captured at last-write (immediately before Phase 6a). Nothing here can run until that artifact exists and is accessible to Backend-Service. The dump is PII-bearing (see item 5) — its storage and access are constrained accordingly.

## Scope — what lands here

1. **Final `mysqldump` dependency (the input).** The capture itself is the wiki#86 / Phase-6 deliverable; this ticket consumes it. It shares its "impossible after 2026-09-07" deadline with the BMI artifact capture in #1500 / #1507 — those should ride the *same* capture pass, so coordinate the dump contents before it is taken. **The capture is now specified in `plans/tubafrenzy-final-dump-capture-spec.md` ([WXYC/wiki#111](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/pull/111)) — that file is the source of truth for what must survive and how to verify it, and Phase 6b step 2 points at it. The list is no longer maintained here.** In brief, the consumers need `BMI_COMPOSER`, `DJ_HANDLE`, `SIGNON_TIME`, `SIGNOFF_TIME`, and both the `FLOWSHEET_ENTRY_PROD.ID` and `ROTATION_RELEASE.ID` keyspaces. Two corrections the spec carries: (a) `FLOWSHEET_RADIO_SHOW_PROD` has **no `START_TIME`** — a show's start is `SIGNON_TIME` and its end is `SIGNOFF_TIME`; `START_TIME` is a `FLOWSHEET_ENTRY_PROD` column, so item 3 reads the former pair; (b) the risk is not a forgotten column but a wrong script — `backup-database.sh` dumps the whole schema so every column survives by construction, while its neighbour `dump-db-for-index-build.sh` omits `ROTATION_RELEASE` and `COMPANY` even in `all` mode.

2. **Ghost-row one-shot sweep** (absorbs #1083). Flowsheet + rotation `legacy_entry_id` ID-set comparison against the final dump: any BS row whose `legacy_entry_id` is absent from the dump's authoritative keyspace is a ghost from a dropped delete-webhook. Logging-only pass first, then batched DELETEs per [`docs/bulk-update-playbook.md`](https://github.com/WXYC/Backend-Service/blob/main/docs/bulk-update-playbook.md) (async-commit + batch-size + `ANALYZE`-after). Do **not** build the recurring reconcile mechanism #1083 originally proposed — the flowsheet + rotation pipe dies at **Phase 3** ([wiki#88](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/88)), not Phase 5; a single sweep against the final dump achieves the same cleanup with none of the machinery. Note that from Phase 3 onward the leak is *total*, not merely widened: the inbound webhooks are cut and both ETLs stop in the same phase, so no tubafrenzy-side delete reaches BS at all between the flip and the final dump. (Phase 2 — [wiki#87](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/87), closed — cut tubafrenzy's *outbound* LML calls only and explicitly left the webhooks pushing.) So the sweep must run against the dump, not against a mid-turndown snapshot.

3. **Stub-show `start_time` repair** (absorbs #1084). One-shot `UPDATE wxyc_schema.shows SET start_time = <dump value> WHERE start_time IS DISTINCT FROM <dump value>` for rows created as `/internal` webhook stubs (which persisted `start_time = NOW()`). Consumers (dj-site, iOS V2, archive, semantic-index) read these times, so the wrong values are user-visible and permanent post-turndown. The one-line ETL conflict-set fix #1084 also proposed is redundant given this sweep repairs every stub at once — skip it.

4. **`BMI_COMPOSER` historical source** (feeds #1500). #1499 shipped the composer worker forward-only, so every pre-2026-06-29 flowsheet row has `composer = NULL`. The dump's `BMI_COMPOSER` column is the *only* historical source of the hand-typed composer credits the BMI performance list needs. Preserve the column in the capture; the backfill decision (whether and how to populate `flowsheet.composer` from it) is made in #1500, not here — this ticket only guarantees the source survives.

5. **PII constraint on the dump** (absorbs #1400's surviving contract; **rule corrected 2026-08-27 — [WXYC/wiki#123](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/123)**). The dump carries DJs' real names in **two** columns: `DJ_NAME` by design, and `DJ_HANDLE` by defect across the whole 22-year corpus (measured: 5,373 of 72,778 shows hold a `DJ_HANDLE` equal to that row's `DJ_NAME`). This item previously stated the rule as "import reads `DJ_HANDLE`, never `DJ_NAME`" — that directed imports at a contaminated column and is withdrawn. The binding rule lives in the capture spec's **PII rule** section ([`plans/tubafrenzy-final-dump-capture-spec.md`](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/blob/main/plans/tubafrenzy-final-dump-capture-spec.md), amended 2026-08-27): restricted storage (`s3://wxyc-archive/` only, never copied to laptops/drives/tickets/repos), and **no import path passes either column through unfiltered** — any value destined for `shows.legacy_dj_name` or another public-reaching surface is re-resolved through the canonical `resolveDjDisplayName` policy or scrubbed to an equivalent standard; the rule is a filter, not a column choice. `wxyc-crm`'s alumni extract legitimately reads real names and is out of the rule's scope. The `shows.legacy_dj_name` → `legacy_dj_handle` rename #1400 floated is a separate Phase-7 schema-cleanup item, not part of this ticket.

## End state

- Ghost flowsheet + rotation rows deleted (with a pre-DELETE log of what was removed).
- `shows.start_time` corrected for every webhook-stub show to its authoritative tubafrenzy value.
- `BMI_COMPOSER` preserved in the retained dump and confirmed available to #1500.
- PII handling rule for the dump documented and, where importable, enforced.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Final dump captured per [the capture spec](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/pull/111) (wiki#86 / Phase 6b step 2), its schema-verification output recorded in the Phase 0 decision log, and accessible to BS with `BMI_COMPOSER`, `DJ_HANDLE`, `SIGNON_TIME`, `SIGNOFF_TIME`, and both the `FLOWSHEET_ENTRY_PROD.ID` and `ROTATION_RELEASE.ID` keyspaces intact.
- [ ] Ghost-row sweep run: log-only diff reviewed, then batched DELETEs executed per the bulk-update playbook, with row counts recorded on this issue.
- [ ] `shows.start_time` repair run: count of rows corrected recorded.
- [ ] #1500 confirms `BMI_COMPOSER` is available as its historical source.
- [ ] Dump PII handling rule recorded per the capture spec's PII rule (amended 2026-08-27, wiki#123); any import path (if built) filters **both** `DJ_NAME` and `DJ_HANDLE` through the canonical `resolveDjDisplayName` policy — neither column is passed through unfiltered.

## Related

- Consolidates the final-dump-keyed residue from #1083 (ghost rows) and #1084 (stub start_times), wired as sub-issues.
- Preservation dependency for #1500 / #1507 (BMI capture rides the same dump pass).
- Carries the surviving PII contract from #1400.
- Turndown decision log: [wiki#86](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/86); org Project #36 (Tubafrenzy decommissioning).



---

_Milestone 1 moved from 2026-08-31 to **2026-09-07** on 2026-08-28 — 24 scheduled DJs still lack a usable Backend account and the classic flowsheet UI is their only surface. Engineering readiness was not the gate. See [WXYC/wiki#125](https://github.com/WXYC/wiki/issues/125)._
